Article Title: Why some Anthropic investors call CEO Dario Amodei 'more of a religious leader than he is a CEO'
Article Text:
The Anthropic IPO is a referendum on whether CEO Dario Amodei doom sells to public investors

Inside Anthropic, a tiny inner circle and a company that asks Claude first

CEO Dario Amodei's AI safety stance has cost Anthropic money

Somebody in the room had a perfectly reasonable idea. Anthropic was mid-way through a historic run, public sentiment around AI was in the gutter, and one director suggested the fix that Microsoft and Facebook reached for during their own boom years—a charm offensive, heavy on drug discovery and cures for hard diseases. Dario Amodei said no. That approach belonged to the past, he argued. The stakes now were more existential.That exchange, reported by The Information, works almost as a thesis statement for how Amodei runs the fastest-growing major company in history. Weeks later, Anthropic's World Cup commercial opened on a row of tombstones and told viewers to ask hard questions about AI. Now, with an IPO expected as soon as September, the 43-year-old has to take that same posture on the road—to money managers who, according to the report, would very much like him to stop frightening everyone.The discomfort isn't new, it's just newly consequential. One Silicon Valley investor wrote down an unusual risk before putting money into Anthropic: he wasn't convinced Amodei actually cared about making money. Others have complained privately that his campaign for AI regulation damages both his company and the wider industry. They also concede they have almost no sway over him.Bill Gurley, who hasn't invested, has called it the most aggressive regulatory capture he's seen.Amodei's allies read the criticism differently—Brad Carson, who runs an Anthropic-backed nonprofit, argues the loudest critics are the ones who can't replicate what he built.Few people close to the company could name a meaningful influence on Amodei beyond his sister and president Daniela, his five other co-founders, and his wife Camilla Clark, a former tech operator with almost no public profile who has never held a role at Anthropic. He leads through long essays and Slack posts, skips most day-to-day management, and holds a twice-monthly all-hands that staff call Dario's Vision Quests—less product review, more state of the world.Employees lean on Claude itself for decisions. Headcount sits above 3,000 and executives don't plan to raise it much, because they'd rather not hire people they'll later have to cut as Claude absorbs internal work. One major investor's summary, per The Information: he is "more of a religious leader than he is a CEO."The conviction has a price tag. When bioweapon classifiers began eating into model margins, the finance team objected and Amodei overruled them. His refusal to accept a Pentagon requirement on permitted uses got Anthropic designated a supply chain risk in March. In June, after a dispute over Fable 5's guardrails, Washington slapped export controls on the model and forced it offline for days.None of it has dented the ascent. Anthropic's valuation has climbed more than 200-fold in three years to $965 billion, and its revenue run rate—estimated recently at $70 billion—passed OpenAI's earlier this year.The compromises are real too: money from Qatar and the UAE, over $1 billion a month paid to Elon Musk's SpaceX for compute. Amodei's own framing, from his January essay, explains the bind better than his critics do. AI, he wrote, is "such a glittering prize" that restraint becomes nearly impossible.
Article Summary: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei's stance on AI has cost the company money. The company's valuation has climbed more than 200-fold in three years to $965 billion. One Silicon Valley investor wrote down an unusual risk before putting money into Anthropic. Others have complained privately that his campaign for AI regulation damages his company.

Article Title: Upset Paramount may leave California; company says it has duty towards shareholders, and that ultimately, you go to the place where you ...
Article Text:
Paramount Skydance and Warner Bros. merger under fire

Jobs and economy

Paramount Skydance reported mixed earnings results

Paramount Skydance’s chief legal officer Makan Delrahim has suggested that the company could leave California as it faces mounting antitrust scrutiny from the state government. According to a report by The Hill, speaking at Politico’s The The California Agenda: Sacramento Summit, Delrahim said CEO David Ellison remains committed to California but emphasized there is a point where the company has a fiduciary duty to shareholders. “You have to take a look at the business environment and look to see what’s best for not only the community and the business. And ultimately, you know, go to the place where you’re wanted,” he said.Paramount, based in Los Angeles, agreed last month to pause its multibillion-dollar acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery after litigation was filed by California’s attorney general and 11 other states. The lawsuit argues the deal would give Paramount excessive power in news, entertainment, and sports media, harming competition. A trial is scheduled for next spring.The merger has drawn criticism from Democrats and media watchdogs, who worry that Warner Bros.Discovery’s CNN could fall under the influence of Ellison, an ally of President Trump and son of Oracle founder Larry Ellison. Ellison defended the deal in a New York Times op-ed, writing: “I do not aspire to lead these companies to bend their newsrooms to my views.”Delrahim argued the lawsuit is harming employment, saying: “This merger is actually going to be good — not only for California — it’ll be good for America.” Paramount maintains that its duty to shareholders may ultimately force it to relocate if California continues to oppose the merger.Recently, Paramount Skydance reported mixed second-quarter results, with revenue rising 1% year-over-year to $6.91 billion, beating estimates, while profit fell short at $41 million. Streaming revenue grew 9% to nearly $2.5 billion, driven by subscriber gains from Paramount+ content including UFC Freedom 250 and the FIFA World Cup. Studio revenue reached $1.3 billion, though theatrical performance lagged compared to last year’s Mission: Impossible — The Final Reckoning.
Article Summary: Paramount Skydance’s chief legal officer Makan Delrahim has suggested that the company could leave California as it faces mounting antitrust scrutiny. Delrahim said CEO David Ellison remains committed to California but emphasized there is a point where the company has a fiduciary duty to shareholders.

Article Title: A robot traveled to Great Pyramid via hidden path and stopped in front of a door that had remained sealed for 4,500 years; here's what happened
Article Text:
Robot explores hidden passage inside Great Pyramid

What did the robot find

Modern technology used to study pyramids

A robot traveled through a hidden passage inside Egypt’s Great Pyramid of Giza and stopped at a sealed barrier that may have remained untouched for about 4,500 years. The discovery has renewed questions about what could be hidden inside the ancient monument. According to an online report, researchers used modern robotic and scanning technology to explore a narrow passage that would be difficult and risky for people to enter. The robot reached the end of the corridor but found a solid wall or sealed doorway. Archaeologists say further study could reveal new details about the pyramid’s design and construction.The Great Pyramid of Giza has been studied for centuries, but scientists still do not know everything about its internal structure. As part of the latest investigation, modern technology was used to examine areas that cannot be easily reached by archaeologists. The robot travelled a 100 feet long passage to a sealed section. The journey ended at a barrier that had remained closed for thousands of years.Instead of finding an open chamber, the robot reached a solid wall or sealed door. The finding has not answered the biggest question surrounding the passage. It has instead created a new one: What is behind the sealed barrier?The area has not been opened, and there has been no confirmed public announcement about what may be on the other side.Egyptologist Zahi Hawass has said that he plans to issue an official report on findings related to the passage after 2026.He has also suggested that a breakthrough of a discovery could radically change our understanding of ancient Egypt.Researchers have increasingly turned to technology to study the Great Pyramid without damaging its ancient stonework. Scientists have used techniques such as thermal imaging, 3D mapping and muon scanning to look inside the massive structure.
Article Summary: Researchers used modern robotic and scanning technology to explore a narrow passage that would be difficult and risky for people to enter. The robot reached the end of the corridor but found a solid wall or sealed doorway. Archaeologists say further study could reveal new details about the pyramid’s design and construction.

Article Title: Google Gemini 3.7 Flash launched for coding, agents: Everything the upgraded model offers
Article Text:
Google has launched Gemini 3.7 flash

Lower API pricing and Google Workspace upgrades

Google has launched Gemini 3.7 Flash, its latest AI model optimised specifically for complex software engineering tasks, web development and autonomous agent workflows. The newest model arrived three weeks after the release of Gemini 3.6 Flash, and the company says that it introduces substantial performance gains in multi-step planning, instruction following and code generation, while debuting at half the per-token introductory price of its predecessor.Major Gains in Coding, Web Design, and Document AnalysisAccording to benchmark results released by Google, Gemini 3.7 Flash delivers marked improvements over the 3.6 model across several technical domains. The company claims that the updated model achieved higher first-pass code accuracy and produced more production-ready code, scoring 43.6% on FrontierCode 1.1 (up from 34.4%) and 65.3% on DeepSWE v1.1 (up from 49.0%).It also said that in UI and web application design, the model demonstrated stronger layout functionality and reference-matching accuracy, earning an Elo score of 1588 compared to 3.6 Flash's 1538 on Arena.ai's WebDev Arena. For complex data processing, for fields like finance, law, and biosciences, Gemini 3.7 Flash significantly outperformed the previous version on document-processing evaluations and real-world business automation tasks.To boost enterprise adoption and scalable deployment of autonomous agents, Google is offering Gemini 3.7 Flash at an introductory price of $0.75 per million input tokens and $3.75 per million output tokens through the end of the year. The company noted that the model is designed to “think more diligently,” requiring less manual developer oversight, fewer retries, and offering better execution during multi-step tool calls.Alongside developer availability via Google's API channels, Gemini 3.7 Flash is being integrated immediately into Gemini Spark, Google's 24/7 personal AI agent available to Google AI Pro and Ultra subscribers in over 160 countries. The update is expected to improve Spark's execution across Google Workspace applications, enhancing accuracy in complex, multi-app workflows.
Article Summary: Google has launched Gemini 3.7 Flash, its latest AI model optimised specifically for complex software engineering tasks, web development and autonomous agent workflows. The newest model arrived three weeks after the release of Gemini. 3.6 Flash, and the company says that it introduces substantial performance gains in multi-step planning, instruction following and code generation.

Article Title: It's one year to Intel becoming a 'US government company', what has this meant for the chip giant
Article Text:
What government ownership means for Intel: Some good and some not-so-good things

The US government became the largest single shareholder in Intel on August 22, 2025, after announcing an $8.9 billion agreement to acquire a 9.9% equity stake (433.3 million shares) in the company. It's been almost a year since then. In what can be called as an unprecedented shift in the US industrial policy, the federal government acquired an approximate 10% equity stake in Intel Corporation, instantly becoming the semiconductor giant’s largest single shareholder.The transaction is part of a broader, sweeping initiative in which Washington is taking equity positions in 30 publicly traded companies spanning key economic sectors. By taking a direct ownership position in Intel—a flagship U.S. chipmaker with a market capitalization of approximately $491.9 billion—the government is signaling a fundamentally new approach to supporting and securing critical national technology infrastructure. Intel forms a key piece in the administration’s effort to restore the U.S.’s domestic manufacturing capacity. Earlier this year, the US President Donald Trump said that he should have asked for a bigger stake in Intel given its newfound success.“I said, ‘Give the country 10% ownership for free in Intel,’” Trump told Fortune Magazine in a May interview. “(Tan) said, ‘You have a deal.’ I said, ‘S—, I should have asked for more.’”The move marked a transformative moment for Intel as it works to execute a turnaround focused on next-generation AI architecture and contract foundry services. As the company competes against global heavyweights like Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. (TSMC) and Nvidia, a backed-by-Washington status could serve as a powerful differentiator.For government agencies and defense contractors with sensitive computing workloads, a federally backed domestic supplier offers crucial supply-chain security and geopolitical reliability. The government's backing strengthens Intel’s core narrative: Positioning itself as a trusted, long-term provider of critical compute infrastructure where supply chain resilience is paramount.However, the unprecedented ownership structure has immediately raised concerns among Wall Street analysts and corporate governance experts. Government involvement introduces novel questions regarding potential political interference, regulatory conflicts of interest, and capital allocation.Intel is already navigating significant execution risks, including massive capital expenditure plans and a recent $20 billion share offering. Investors worry that sovereign ownership could slow down decision-making, entangle the company in bureaucracy, or force policy-driven trade-offs at the expense of shareholder returns.Industry observers note that the federal intervention in Intel could set a wide-reaching precedent. As governments worldwide rush to secure domestic hardware capacity for artificial intelligence, Washington's move may herald a permanent shift toward state-backed corporate partnerships across the broader AI infrastructure landscape.
Article Summary: The US government became the largest single shareholder in Intel on August 22, 2025. Washington announced an $8.9 billion agreement to acquire a 9.9% equity stake in the company. The move marked a transformative moment for Intel as it works to execute a turnaround.

Article Title: As Google search result shows Sam Altman dead, company clarifies not their fault; says: This was not a manual change by Google, it is when ...
Article Text:
Google has removed incorrect information about Sam Altman

Google removes incorrect information about Sam Altman

Wikipedia page reportedly targeted by vandals

Similar false claim against Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei

Google briefly displayed incorrect search results claiming that OpenAI CEO Sam Altman had died, triggering confusion and jokes across social media before the company removed the information. The false result appeared on August 12 after users on Reddit and X (formerly known as Twitter) shared screenshots showing Google's search page stating that Altman had died that day. Google later confirmed the information was incorrect and said it was not the result of a manual change by the company.The incorrect search result quickly went viral after users posted screenshots on Reddit and X. Google removed the incorrect information within hours. In an X post, Google said the issue has been fixed.“Thanks for flagging - this is no longer appearing, and was not a manual change by Google,” the company said adding “When people vandalize public info sources, this can affect the information that appears in Search”.The company did not identify the specific source that caused the incorrect information to appear.According to SBS News, the incident is believed to be linked to vandalism on Sam Altman's English Wikipedia page.The report said the page's revision history showed several false edits, including claims that Altman had been assassinated and changes to his surname from "Altman" to "Gayman."Following the incident, Wikipedia reportedly restricted editing of the page, allowing only registered users to make changes in an effort to prevent further vandalism.A similar incident is now affecting Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei. Users on social media reported that results on Google Search are showing incorrect information suggesting Amodei had died.
Article Summary: Google briefly displayed incorrect search results claiming that OpenAI CEO Sam Altman had died. The false result appeared on August 12 after users on Reddit and X (formerly known as Twitter) shared screenshots showing Google's search page. Google later confirmed the information was incorrect and said it was not the result of a manual change by the company. Google removed the incorrect information within hours.

Article Text:
Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg: ‘Merab made me take my shirt off’

Mark Zuckerberg’s well-known MMA habit

The yacht controversy

Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg has taken his mixed martial arts training to new heights or rather new waters by sparring with former UFC bantamweight champion Merab Dvalishvili on a giant barge in the middle of Lake Tahoe. In a one-minute-plus video shared on Instagram, the pair traded blows in front of drones, videographers, and friends, with Zuckerberg’s wife Priscilla Chan casually paddling past on a canoe.Zuckerberg also joked in the one-minute clip that Dvalishvili insisted that he remove his shirt ‘because it looks more fighter.’ While the UFC star appeared to be going easy on the billionaire, Zuckerberg showcased striking and wrestling skills, even throwing Dvalishvili into the water. The sparring session marks the second time the duo have trained together, following a December 2025 meet-up.The footage captured multiple angles of the sparring rounds, with an array of cameras clearly set up in advance to document the encounter. At one point, Zuckerberg's wife Priscilla Chan is seen paddling past the barge on a canoe. Sharing the clip, Zuckerberg explained that Dvalishvili had told him to take his shirt off because it looks more fighter.Dvalishvili, who won the UFC bantamweight title in 2024 and remains the division's top contender, appeared to go easy on the tech billionaire throughout the session. Even so, Zuckerberg got a moment to show off his striking and wrestling, at one point throwing Dvalishvili into the lake. This marks the second time the pair have sparred publicly, having first done rounds together in December 2025.Zuckerberg has built a reputation over the past few years for training regularly in MMA and jiujitsu, often sparring with some of the sport's most accomplished fighters. His dedication to the sport previously prompted UFC president Dana White to remark that the Meta boss could hold his own physically against just about anyone.The viral fight comes as Zuckerberg faces scrutiny over his $300 million yacht Launchpad, which was accused of ignoring a distress call from a stranded vessel in Alaskan waters earlier this month. Mark Zuckerberg’s $390 million, 387-foot yacht Launchpad was recently booed over a reported failure to respond to a stranded boat. A Meta spokesperson has now clarified that the vessel's crew was on a different radio channel and that help was already on the way. The incident happened last Monday, August 3 evening in Alaska after a 21-foot skiff ran out of fuel between Juneau and Petersburg. While social media users criticised Mark Zuckerberg's superyacht, the company said neither Zuckerberg nor his family were on board at the time.

Article Title: Months before moving away from CEO role at Google Deepmind, Demis Hassabis met officials in Trump administration to discuss safety of ...
Article Text:
Demis Hassabis’ meeting with US officials

Leadership transition at Google

Months before moving away from his role as CEO of Google DeepMind, Demis Hassabis held discussions with Trump administration officials and leaders of other AI labs about forming a new independent industry safety body. According to a report by Wall Street Journal, people familiar to the matter revealed that Hassabis has been advancing the idea of an organization that would codify safety guardrails and best practices for developing artificial general intelligence (AGI). He has likened the proposed entity to the International Atomic Energy Agency, a nongovernmental watchdog for nuclear energy.The report further adds that earlier this summer, Hassabis met with Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and Trump tech adviser Michael Kratsios to preview aspects of his plan. He later published an essay on X calling for a U.S.-led, industry-funded standards body to assess AI models, similar to the Financial Industry Regulatory Authority. Under his proposal, federal agencies and national laboratories would work with AI companies to test models relevant to national security and designate “frontier-class” systems.The world’s largest AI labs are racing toward AGI, but leaders including Hassabis, Sam Altman of OpenAI, and Dario Amodei of Anthropic have voiced concerns about risks.Altman recently proposed a U.S.-led international forum, while Anthropic endorsed a global agreement to slow development and verify compliance. Hassabis’s efforts represent some of the most concrete steps by a leading lab official to establish safety mechanisms.Last week, Google announced a management shake-up at DeepMind, with Hassabis stepping down as CEO and becoming chairman of DeepMind and chief scientist of Alphabet. In a memo, he wrote: “I’ve been working towards AGI my whole life and now, like many of you, I feel it is close at hand… I’ve decided that now is the right time to hand over my day-to-day operational responsibilities.” Alphabet CEO Sundar Pichai said Hassabis’s new role allows him to focus fully on shaping the future of AGI.Critics argue voluntary and self-regulatory efforts are insufficient to address AI’s security and economic risks. Lawmakers are calling for mandatory model reviews and stronger government oversight. The Trump administration has increased scrutiny of AI’s security risks but continues to keep evaluations voluntary, leaving the debate over regulation unresolved as AGI development accelerates.
Article Summary: Demis Hassabis held discussions with US officials and leaders of other AI labs about forming a new independent industry safety body. He has likened the proposed entity to the International Atomic Energy Agency, a nongovernmental watchdog for nuclear energy. He later published an essay on X calling for a U.S.-led, industry-funded standards body to assess AI models.

Article Title: How AI boom has helped Microsoft keep a window open in China, a market that the company almost left nine years ago
Article Text:
Microsoft’s shift from government vendor to global enterprise partner

How Microsoft navigated engineering talent and export restrictions

Microsoft, which almost exited the market a decade ago, is using the global appetite for artificial intelligence (AI) and cloud infrastructure services to stay in China amid heightened geopolitical tensions and more competition from local players. While competitors like Google exited the mainland market years ago over censorship and security concerns, Microsoft maintained deep connections with Chinese leadership and enterprise clients, as per a report by news agency Reuters.However, corporate filings reveal that over the past five years, Microsoft has closed at least 15 branch offices and joint ventures across China. Citing company sources, the report claims that executives internally weighed a full market exit in 2023 due to expanding geopolitical risks, particularly with China accounting for roughly 1.5% of the tech giant’s global revenue.Despite those deliberations, Microsoft elected to remain, pivoting its regional business model to serve Chinese enterprise giants expanding overseas.Microsoft’s early strategy centered heavily on serving Chinese state enterprises and government agencies, going so far as to launch a specialised “Windows 10 China Government Edition” in 2017 following personal negotiations between CEO Satya Nadella and Chinese ministry officials.However, Beijing’s push for software self-sufficiency and tough cyber procurement rules introduced in 2017 gradually tipped the scales in favor of domestic software alternatives to foreign operating systems.Microsoft responded by focusing its primary attention on servicing Chinese private companies with global operations, such as TikTok owner ByteDance and online retailer Shein.These companies store user data around the world in Microsoft's Azure cloud infrastructure, complying with Western rules. Additionally, Azure offers Chinese enterprise clients access to global AI models, allowing Microsoft to build its largest China-linked business around enabling domestic firms to scale overseas.Beyond cloud services, access to elite software engineering talent remains a core driver of Microsoft’s continued presence in the region. Established in the late 1990s, Microsoft Research Asia (MSRA) served as a foundational incubator for Chinese technology leaders, with alumni going on to help found major artificial intelligence companies across the country.To avoid regulatory restrictions, Microsoft moved the MSRA branch to Vancouver, Singapore and Tokyo, taking key research projects involving sensitive technologies such as quantum computing out of mainland China.
Article Summary: Microsoft has closed at least 15 branch offices and joint ventures across China over the past five years. The tech giant is using the global appetite for artificial intelligence (AI) and cloud infrastructure services to stay in China. China accounts for roughly 1.5% of the tech giant's global revenue.

Article Title: Chinese company that made Apple seek ‘special permission’ from the US government becomes country's most valuable firm
Article Text:
CXMT becomes China's most valuable company

Market shift from internet giants to silicon leadership

Tencent faces pressure over escalating AI spending

Chipmaker ChangXin Memory Technologies (CXMT) has officially overtaken internet giant Tencent Holdings Ltd. to become China’s most valuable company, signaling a dramatic market shift toward artificial intelligence hardware and semiconductor self-sufficiency. CXMT maintained a market capitalisation of $524 billion, surpassing Hong Kong-listed Tencent, whose valuation slid to $510 billion amid investor scrutiny over its rising AI expenditures, according to a report by Bloomberg.Headquartered in Hefei, Anhui province, CXMT has emerged as a primary vehicle for investor bets on China’s domestic chip production capabilities. The company ranks as the world’s fourth-largest manufacturer of dynamic random-access memory (DRAM), which has become a vital component that is utilised across smartphones, consumer electronics and high-performance AI data servers.Following a 467% surge during its Shanghai stock exchange debut last month, CXMT shares have climbed an additional 8%, cementing its status as China’s largest onshore-listed firm. Market analysts noted that the valuation crossover reflects changing priorities across global equity markets.“CXMT exceeding Tencent is a message from the market — chips are the new clicks. Our sense is the gap between the two will widen as agentic AI takes an increasing share of internet flows,” Gary Tan, a portfolio manager at Allspring Global Investments, was quoted as saying.The chipmaker reportedly made Apple seek special permission from the US government before considering its memory chips for some products due to US export restrictions.While CXMT benefits from the hardware boom, Tencent has struggled to maintain its valuation lead. Shares of the Shenzhen-based tech giant, which operates the ubiquitous WeChat messaging ecosystem and owns major video game studios including Riot Games, have fallen more than 26% this year.
Article Summary: ChangXin Memory Technologies (CXMT) has officially overtaken internet giant Tencent Holdings Ltd. to become China’s most valuable company. CXMT maintained a market capitalisation of $524 billion, surpassing Tencent, whose valuation slid to $510 billion amid investor scrutiny over rising AI expenditures.

Article Title: Trump memo to government organisations: Partner private technology companies to conduct cyber attacks against criminal groups and foreign adversaries
Article Text:
Trump enlisting private sector innovation against cybercrime

Financial safeguards put in place

US President Donald Trump has signed a national security presidential memorandum, allowing federal law enforcement agencies to partner with private technology companies to execute offensive cyber operations against foreign criminal groups and international adversaries. The White House stated that the directive aims to give federal authorities broader capabilities to dismantle Transnational Criminal Organisations (TCOs) that pose a growing threat to American citizens, businesses and national security.Under the new policy framework, vetted private sector technology firms will be permitted to work under direct federal supervision to propose, coordinate and execute targeted cyber actions.“These organisations conduct sustained cyber campaigns to perpetrate frauds that undermine American prosperity, security, and freedom,” the memo said, adding, “It is the policy of the US to use all instruments of national power, including the innovative capabilities of the private sector, to combat cybercrime.”The White House fact sheet accompanying the memorandum highlighted widespread ransomware campaigns, financial fraud schemes and cross-border cyber extortion.To counter these threats, the memorandum directs the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) through the National Coordination Center within the Homeland Security Task Force to establish a specialised operational program.The initiative will be jointly overseen by DHS and the Department of Justice (DOJ), creating a formal bridge between public law enforcement and private technology contractors. Under the framework private firms can form collaborative agreements with federal, state, local, tribal and territorial agencies to collect threat intelligence on foreign networks.Secondly, vetted private partners will be authorised to conduct both “cyber surveillance operations” and “cyber effects operations” against approved foreign targets. The memo defines “cyber effects” as actions that manipulate, disrupt, deny, degrade or destroy digital infrastructure, information systems and physical hardware controlled by targeted organisations.To ensure accountability and prevent unauthorised activity, participating companies will be required to pass rigorous vetting processes and maintain a financial bond or escrow account of at least $1 million. While the Trump administration framed the partnership as a necessary evolution in national defense, the concept of utilising private technology contractors for offensive digital operations has drawn debate among cybersecurity policy experts.
Article Summary: US President Donald Trump has signed a national security presidential memorandum. It allows federal law enforcement agencies to partner with private technology companies to execute offensive cyber operations against foreign criminal groups and international adversaries. To ensure accountability and prevent unauthorised activity, participating companies will be required to pass rigorous vetting processes.

Article Title: Google Fitbit Air India launch in October, company confirms: All you need to know
Article Text:
Minimalist design built for constant wear

Google Fitbit Air India listing

Google officially confirmed on Thursday (August 13) that its first screen-free fitness wearable, the Fitbit Air, will launch in India in October 2026. The announcement arrived during a briefing following the annual “Made by Google” keynote, where the company unveiled its flagship hardware portfolio, including the Google Pixel 11 smartphone lineup, the Pixel 11 Pro Fold and the Pixel Watch 5 in India. In the US, the company has also launched Pixel Tag Bluetooth tracker. While Google did not disclose exact Indian pricing, retailer availability or launch date, it showcased the Fitbit Air at the India event.Originally launched in select global markets in May for $99.99 (approximately Rs 9,400), the Fitbit Air introduces a screenless form factor designed to eliminate screen-induced distractions and notification fatigue. The tracker focuses purely on passive health telemetry and background data collection.According to Google, it can continuously monitor heart rate, resting heart rate, heart rate variability (HRV), and irregular heart rhythm (AFib) as well as blood oxygen (SpO2) alongside automated sleep cycle tracking. Global purchases include a complimentary three-month trial to Google Health Premium and access to AI-powered Google Health Coach tools.Recently, third-party listings for the Fitbit Air surfaced on Amazon India, offering early pricing indicators. On the e-commerce platform, the fitness tracker appeared via third-party sellers with prices ranging from Rs 17,380 for the black Performance Loop variant to Rs. 18,490 for the pink model. Official retail pricing directly from Google is expected closer to the October rollout.Internationally, the Fitbit Air supports three distinct interchangeable strap designs: the lightweight Performance Loop Band, the water-resistant Active Band, and the premium Elevated Modern Band.
Article Summary: Google confirms Fitbit Air will launch in India in October 2026. The fitness tracker is Google's first screen-free fitness wearable. It was launched in select global markets in May for $99.99 (approximately Rs 9,400) Google did not disclose Indian pricing, retailer availability or launch date.

Article Title: Quote of the day by Sundar Pichai: “When you have the choice to work on something hard, say yes”
Article Text:
Quote of the day by Sundar Pichai: Meaning and significance

The lesson from Google Chrome

Persistence helped change the outcome

Choosing challenges can expand your limits

What Sundar Pichai's quote means for everyday life

Sundar Pichai's three filters for making choices

Why excitement matters alongside difficulty

The bigger message behind the quote

Google and Alphabet CEO Sundar Pichai has built much of his career around taking on difficult problems and pushing technology into new areas. In his 2026 commencement address at Stanford University, Sundar Pichai shared a simple lesson with the graduating Class of 2026: “When you have the choice to work on something hard, say yes. ” The advice came as part of three personal filters he said had helped him make better decisions throughout his life. Sundar Pichai argued that difficult work can bring together talented and optimistic people, create opportunities to learn and produce meaningful results even when the original goal is not fully achieved. His own experience working on Google Chrome became one of the clearest examples of why he believes challenging problems are worth pursuing.Sundar Pichai's message is not simply about choosing the most difficult task available. Instead, he encourages people to recognise opportunities where the challenge itself can lead to growth. In his Stanford commencement speech, Sundar Pichai said that working on hard things can bring talented and optimistic people together. He also noted that even when people fail to meet the ambitious goals they set, they can still achieve something meaningful.For Sundar Pichai, the value of taking on a difficult challenge is not always limited to the final outcome. Such experiences can teach people how to solve unfamiliar problems, work with others, develop new skills and continue moving forward when early results are disappointing.Sundar Pichai used the development of Google Chrome to demonstrate what he meant by working on difficult problems. After joining Google in 2004, he eventually became involved in a project aimed at reimagining the web browser. At the time, there was an internal consensus that creating a competitive browser would be extremely difficult and would require hundreds of engineers. The group working on the project, however, consisted of about 10 people. Sundar Pichai acknowledged that the team was somewhat naive about how difficult the challenge would be, but that willingness to attempt something ambitious helped drive the project forward.The early story of Chrome also shows why difficult work requires persistence. Google launched Chrome in 2008 and received strong initial interest. Sundar Pichai recalled that the browser attracted about eight million users within its first 24 hours and received positive reviews. But the momentum soon slowed. After a year, Chrome had around 2% market share, and Microsoft CEO Steve Ballmer publicly dismissed the browser as a “rounding error”. For the team, this could have been a reason to abandon the project. Instead, Sundar Pichai said they continued working towards aggressive goals and focused on improving the product.The Chrome team continued to iterate rapidly, according to Sundar Pichai. He said the team released new versions roughly every six weeks, while competitors sometimes took six months to a year between releases. The strategy eventually began to pay off as Chrome's success grew. Sundar Pichai's account highlights an important part of his quote: choosing difficult work does not mean success will arrive immediately. A challenging project can initially produce disappointing results, criticism or uncertainty. What matters is whether the challenge is meaningful enough to keep improving and learning from what is not working.Another important part of Sundar Pichai's message was his view of failure. He told Stanford graduates that even if they failed to meet the high goals they had set, they could still achieve something great. This approach takes some of the pressure away from ambitious decisions. A person may begin a project with a particular target, only to discover that the target is unrealistic or that circumstances have changed. That does not necessarily mean the effort was wasted. The skills gained, relationships developed and lessons learned during the process can become valuable in future opportunities.Sundar Pichai's advice also challenges the instinct to choose the safest option every time. Difficult work often requires people to operate outside familiar territory. It may involve learning something completely new, dealing with uncertainty or collaborating with people who have different expertise. Those experiences can gradually expand a person's understanding of what they are capable of doing. For students and young professionals in particular, choosing a meaningful challenge can provide experiences that are difficult to gain from staying entirely within a comfort zone.The quote does not mean people should deliberately make their lives harder. There is a difference between unnecessary difficulty and a worthwhile challenge. Sundar Pichai's advice is better understood as an encouragement not to reject a valuable opportunity simply because it appears difficult. If a project can provide an opportunity to learn, create something useful or solve a meaningful problem, its difficulty may be a reason to consider it rather than a reason to walk away. The important question is not simply, “Is this hard?” but “Is this challenge worth taking on?”The advice about difficult work was one part of three filters Sundar Pichai shared during his Stanford commencement address. His first was to choose optimism, which he described as a way of reframing circumstances and looking for positive possibilities. His second was to gravitate towards working on hard things. His third was to do the thing that excites you when all other factors are equal. Sundar Pichai said these filters had helped him navigate decisions and take some of the pressure out of moments that can otherwise feel overwhelming.Sundar Pichai's third filter adds an important qualification to his advice about hard work. He did not suggest pursuing difficult projects simply because they are difficult. He encouraged graduates to consider what genuinely excites them. For Sundar Pichai, that interest has long been connected to technology and its ability to improve people's lives. He recalled seeing computers at Stanford and becoming fascinated by the possibilities of the internet. That interest later influenced his decision to join Google and work on products including Chrome, Chromebooks and Android.At its core, Sundar Pichai's message is about how people respond to uncertainty. Life rarely provides a guarantee that a difficult choice will lead to success. Some projects will work, others will fail and many will take unexpected turns. But avoiding every difficult opportunity can also mean missing chances to learn and grow. Sundar Pichai's own experience with Chrome illustrates this idea. What began as a project that many considered extremely difficult eventually became one of Google's major products. His advice to graduates was therefore straightforward: when a meaningful opportunity requires you to stretch your abilities, do not automatically step away because it is hard. Sometimes, saying yes to the difficult path can open the door to possibilities you could not see at the beginning.
Article Summary: Sundar Pichai shared a simple lesson with the graduating Class of 2026: “When you have the choice to work on something hard, say yes ” The advice came as part of three personal filters he said had helped him make better decisions throughout his life. He argued that difficult work can bring together talented and optimistic people, create opportunities to learn and produce meaningful results.

Article Title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang on AI bloodbath fears: people confuse jobs with tasks; says AI will not eliminate jobs, it will actually…
Article Text:
Jensen Huang, CEO, Nvidia.

Jensen Huang's tasks-versus-jobs case rests on radiologists who never went away

The AI job loss numbers don't quite match the Nvidia CEO's optimism

Why Sam Altman, Dario Amodei, and every AI boss suddenly sounds like Jensen Huang on jobs

Jensen Huang has a problem with how the AI jobs debate is being conducted, and it starts with vocabulary. Speaking at Y Combinator's Startup School, the Nvidia CEO said the people forecasting a white-collar bloodbath keep using two words interchangeably that mean very different things. A task is one thing you do. A job is a purpose you serve, and it holds dozens of tasks inside it. AI is extremely good at swallowing the first. It has shown almost no ability to swallow the second.That distinction is the whole of his argument. "The narrative of AI destroying jobs is exactly backward," Huang said, predicting that every role will change and a fresh batch of roles will appear alongside. It is a direct shot at the most-quoted AI prediction of the past 18 months—Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei's warning that AI could erase half of entry-level white-collar jobs—and Huang has spent months sharpening it across stages in Los Angeles, Washington and now Silicon Valley.His clearest example of a task is the customer service worker who takes a complaint and reads back an answer from a database. Huang expects that to be automated, and it already is. Uber cut 10% of its customer support staff in July and pointed at exactly this technology.Radiology is where he flips the argument. Machines read scans now, the one task that was supposed to end the profession. Radiologist hiring kept rising anyway, and Huang's reasoning is the patient backlog—clear the scans faster and hospitals simply admit more people.Software engineering runs on the same logic. Coders now spend less time writing code and more time directing tools like Claude Code and Codex, while demand for engineers grows. The queue of things companies want built was never the constraint.Huang also cited legal AI startup Harvey, claiming paralegal hiring is growing like crazy rather than collapsing. That is the weakest link in the chain. The US Bureau of Labor Statistics projects little or no change in paralegal employment through 2034.He made a similar pitch on Axios' "Behind the Curtain" in July, dismissing the half-of-all-jobs forecast as "complete nonsense" and holding up the data centre boom as a manufacturing revival. Manufacturing employment is still below its post-pandemic peak. Data centre construction jobs are temporary by design, and the finished buildings run on skeleton crews. The wider research sits somewhere between the two camps—recent studies suggest AI is changing how people work without displacing them at scale, while hiring for fresh graduates has visibly stalled.Huang's deeper worry is reputational. At a Milken Institute event in May he said his greatest concern is scaring people so badly with science-fiction stories that they refuse to engage with AI at all. He would rather frame it as America's best shot at re-industrialising.He is no longer the outlier. Sam Altman said in May he was delighted to be wrong about AI eating entry-level work. Amodei recalibrated too, though he still treats some job loss as intrinsic. Mark Zuckerberg 's 6,500-word essay on Monday promised an "abundance of jobs," a world with smaller companies in far greater numbers, and new careers like one-person-studio designers, world builders and personal biologists. Meta has put $115 million into a five-week academy that trains data centre technicians and hands them a job at the end.The timing deserves a mention. Anthropic filed confidentially for an IPO in June, public sentiment on AI has cratered, and doom that once sold beautifully to a tech press hungry for big claims sells terribly to retail investors.What separates Huang from the rest is that his claim can actually be checked. If tasks keep disappearing while headcount keeps climbing, he wins the argument. Two years of hiring data will settle it.
Article Summary: Jensen Huang, CEO of Nvidia, says AI is good at swallowing tasks but not jobs. He says people are using two words interchangeably that mean very different things. Huang has spent months sharpening it across stages in Los Angeles, Washington and now Silicon Valley.

Article Title: Why $100 Android phones are quietly disappearing from US shelves
Article Text:
America's cheapest Android phones are disappearing quietly

Scale is the only defence left against rising memory prices

The cheapest Android phones in America are disappearing, and almost nobody is announcing it. Sales of sub-$100 smartphones in the US collapsed 64% year-on-year in Q2 2026, according to Counterpoint Research's US Smartphone Channel Share Tracker. Some brands stopped shipping these devices altogether. Others quietly raised prices until the phones were no longer cheap.The culprit sits inside the phone. Hyperscalers buying up RAM for AI data centres have pushed memory costs sharply higher, and at the bottom of the market there is no margin to absorb that. Add fuel and grocery price increases tied to Middle East conflicts, and the buyer most sensitive to a $30 swing simply stopped upgrading. Overall US smartphone sales fell 5% in the quarter.The split is stark. The Big Four—Apple, Samsung, Motorola and Google—saw combined sales dip just 4%. Everyone else fell 45%. Larger players can lock in component inventory at volumes smaller brands cannot touch, a gap that widened after tariff worries and a soft prepaid market pushed several names out in 2025. HMD exited the US entirely last year.Carrier white-label handsets have been hit hardest, because the price gap that justified their existence has all but closed.Prepaid sales dropped 11%, yet Samsung and Motorola grew their share of it, leaning on Galaxy A and Moto G models to catch switchers.That has created something odd. The $200-300 band, long a dead zone in the US, nearly tripled in share as Motorola moved its top G Series phones up into it. Samsung added $50 to the Galaxy A17 in July.Expect more of the same. Apple's iPhone 18 is widely expected to launch dearer, and Google's Pixel 11 already starts above the Pixel 10.
Article Summary: Sales of sub-$100 smartphones in the US collapsed 64% year-on-year in Q2 2026. Some brands stopped shipping these devices altogether. Others quietly raised prices until the phones were no longer cheap. The culprit sits inside the phone. Hyperscalers buying up RAM for AI data centres have pushed memory costs sharply higher.

Article Title: Chinese smartphone brands lose shine in India market: What is making the old playbook that they had mastered for over 10 years impossible to follow
Article Text:
Chinese smartphone brands In India

What exactly is hurting Chinese smartphone brands in India

Chinese smartphone brands: Down, but no way they are out

India’s smartphone market was once almost synonymous with Chinese brands. Xiaomi, Vivo, Oppo, realme and OnePlus systematically dismantled the old order by offering more specifications for less money, selling aggressively online and launching new models at a pace few rivals could match.That dominance is now showing cracks. IDC’s latest numbers underline how quickly the market is changing. Smartphone shipments in India fell 11.1% year-on-year to 33.2 million units in the April-June quarter of 2026. But the pain was distributed unevenly: Vivo shipments fell 13.9%, Xiaomi 10%, Oppo 8.5% and realme 14.2%. Poco declined 12.3%, while iQOO suffered a staggering 61% fall. Samsung and Apple, in contrast, managed marginal shipment growth despite a shrinking overall market.The bigger problem for Chinese brands is that the part of the Indian smartphone market they mastered is precisely the part now under the greatest pressure. Rising memory and other component costs are destroying the economics of cheap smartphones. IDC says the average selling price (ASP) reached a record $315 in Q2, while the sub-$100 segment collapsed. The shift was already visible in Q1, when IDC said rising memory prices, higher device prices and cautious consumer spending were weighing on demand.For years, Chinese brands prospered by compressing margins and stuffing increasingly powerful hardware into Rs 10,000-20,000 phones. That formula becomes considerably harder when component prices rise. Consumers either postpone purchases or move up the price ladder — where Apple and Samsung have much stronger brands.Xiaomi once disrupted India's smartphone market, but the very proposition that made it successful — aggressive specifications at aggressive prices — has become harder to sustain. Xiaomi wants to premiumise, but convincing a consumer who remembers it as the king of Rs 10,000 phones to spend Rs 50,000 or more is a much tougher job than simply putting premium hardware inside a premium phone.The company is now expanding aggressively beyond smartphones, including launching its Mijia home-appliance brand in India. That may make strategic sense, but it also illustrates how its smartphone business no longer has the swagger it once did.OnePlus faces an even more fundamental identity problem. It entered India as the enthusiast’s “flagship killer”: clean software, powerful specifications and premium performance without premium pricing. Over time, it moved upmarket, broadened its portfolio and became increasingly intertwined with Oppo. In the process, the proposition became less distinctive. A brand built on being the clever alternative to expensive flagships now sells expensive flagships itself.That is a dangerous place to be. At Rs 50,000-70,000, consumers are no longer comparing processor benchmarks alone. They are buying ecosystem, cameras, resale value, service, software longevity and brand status — areas where Samsung and Apple possess formidable advantages. Internationally too, OnePlus has dramatically scaled back operations in several Western markets, adding to questions about what the brand ultimately wants to be.There is another structural shift hurting Chinese vendors: India is becoming less online-centric. IDC data shows online smartphone shipments fell 19.8% in Q2, compared with only a 3.6% decline offline. That is particularly damaging for brands whose rise was built around flash sales, e-commerce exclusives and spec-sheet comparisons.None of this means Chinese brands are disappearing. Vivo remains a market leader and Realme too is doing quite well. Chinese companies collectively still sell tens of millions of phones in India.But their old playbook is losing potency. Even separate Counterpoint data shows their collective share falling to its lowest level for a second calendar quarter since 2020, largely because of their dependence on entry- and mid-priced smartphones.India's smartphone market is moving from “how much phone can I get for my money?” to “which phone is worth spending more money on?” Chinese brands won the first battle spectacularly. Winning the second will be considerably harder. It needs restrategising and innovation, offering a value that goes beyond just specs. It may be User Experience, After-sales service, Upgrade offers or more. The brands that have been dominating the Indian smartphone market for over a decade now need to figure it out. The next few months will tell where and how much they succeed.
Article Summary: Smartphone shipments in India fell 11.1% year-on-year to 33.2 million units in the April-June quarter of 2026. Vivo shipments fell 13.9%, Xiaomi 10%, Oppo 8.5% and realme 14.2%. Poco declined 12.3%, while iQOO suffered a staggering 61% fall.

Article Title: Jeff Bezos is reportedly buying a house in Beverly Hills that is five times the price of any condo ever sold in LA, why this billionaire buy is ‘odd’
Article Text:
Jeff Bezos may be in talks to purchase stake in Liverpool FC

Why Jeff Bezos ’ Beverly Hills condo purchase is unusual

What Jeff Bezos reportedly gets for the price

Aman declines to confirm buyer's identity

Amazon founder Jeff Bezos is reportedly buying a six-bedroom Condo in Beverly Hills, Los Angeles. According to a report by The Hollywood Reporter, the Condo is located at the soon-to-open Aman residence-and-hotel complex. It costs $12,000-per-square foot and is said to be “the most expensive condo ever sold in L.A”.If the reported purchase goes through, it would not only become the most expensive condo ever sold in Los Angeles, but also one of the costliest residential property deals in the city's history. The reported asking price of $200 million is about five times higher than the previous record for a Los Angeles condominium sale, making the deal unusual even by billionaire standards.According to the report, the Aman Beverly Hills project is still under construction and is expected to open in 2028. Located near Rodeo Drive, the development will combine luxury residences with a five-star Aman hotel, offering homeowners access to hotel-style services and amenities.According to The Hollywood Reporter, the reported six-bedroom penthouse spans about 17,000 square feet and is one of just two mirror-image residences on the top floor of the building. The residence is expected to feature 22-foot ceilings, a private cinema, a gym, multiple kitchens, yoga decks, and a rooftop with a 65-foot swimming pool and Jacuzzi.Owners will also have access to the adjoining Aman hotel, including its spa, restaurants, luxury retail stores and a 10-acre botanical garden.The Aman residence-and-hotel complex did not confirm whether Bezos is the buyer, the report says. It quotes a company spokesperson as saying, "For privacy reasons, Aman does not disclose the identities of buyers of Aman Residences."However, the publication also cited a source with direct knowledge of Bezos' real estate dealings who said the Amazon founder had not made such a purchase, leaving the reported deal unconfirmed.
Article Summary: Amazon founder Jeff Bezos is reportedly buying a six-bedroom condo in Beverly Hills, Los Angeles. The reported asking price of $200 million is about five times higher than the previous record for a Los Angeles condominium sale. The Aman residence-and-hotel complex did not confirm whether Bezos is the buyer.

Article Title: Honor Robot Phone launched with 200MP titanium gimbal camera: Price, specs and everything you need to know
Article Text:
Honor Robot Phone

Honor squeezed a 4DoF gimbal into a 9.6mm phone, and it took 100 patents

Under the arm sits a fairly ordinary 6.3-inch flagship

Honor has finally launched the Robot Phone in China, closing out a tease that started at the Magic8 unveiling last October and ran through a CES prototype and months of leaks. The phone's headline feature is a motorised arm that rises out of the back panel, carrying a 200MP camera on a titanium gimbal that tilts, pans and spins on command.Pricing starts at CNY 9,999 (roughly Rs 1.23 lakh) for the 12GB/512GB model, with the 16GB/1TB version at CNY 12,999 (about Rs 1.6 lakh). Preorders are live and open sales begin on August 18. This is a China-only launch, and Honor has said nothing about India or any other market.Honor claims the industry's smallest 4DoF gimbal system, built across 60 manufacturing processes using more than 100 precision components. The titanium motor weighs 2.6g and measures 6mm thick. The company says the assembly is 65% smaller than mainstream gimbals while being 200% stronger, and it all tucks into a 9.6mm frame—though the phone tips the scales at 248 grams.The gimbal camera pairs a 1/1.28-inch 200MP sensor with an f/1.6 lens. Beside it sit a 200MP periscope telephoto (1/1.4-inch, 62mm) and a 50MP ultrawide. Video tops out at 4K 120fps, or 4K 60fps in LogC3, the format that comes via Honor's tie-up with German cinema camera maker Arri.On-device LUT grading and Arri film profiles are part of the same deal. Spinshot handles 90-degree and 180-degree rotations, and AI subject tracking locks on with a double tap.Honor's Yoyo assistant powers what it calls Robot Mode. The arm nods, shakes its head, dances to music and runs through over 100 expressions. Charming in a demo, certainly. The actual case for spending flagship money still rests on stabilisation and tracking during vlogs, livestreams and video calls. Honor says third-party developers will get access to the gimbal and perception stack.Pull the arm out of the equation and what's left is a compact flagship. The 6.3-inch LTPO OLED runs at 2640x1216 with a 1-120Hz refresh range and a peak local brightness of 6,800 nits, which is among the highest figures quoted on any phone this year. Honor has layered its AR anti-reflective coating on top, a sensible addition on a device meant to be used outdoors with the camera arm extended. The display is small by 2026 flagship standards—useful, given the phone already weighs 248 grams before you factor in a case.Powering it is Qualcomm's Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 with a custom cooling setup, running alongside Honor's own H1 imaging chip that handles the tracking and stabilisation work. Configurations go up to 16GB of RAM and 1TB of storage. The 7,060mAh silicon-carbon battery is generous for a 9.6mm frame, and it supports 120W wired and 50W wireless charging—welcome, since a motorised gimbal and 4K 120fps recording will drain a cell faster than a normal camera app. Software is MagicOS 10 on Android 16, and the phone comes in Silver and Gray.
Article Summary: The Honor Robot Phone has a motorised gimbal that tilts, pans and spins on command. Under the arm sits a fairly ordinary 6.3-inch flagship display. The phone is priced at CNY 9,999 (roughly Rs 1.23 lakh) for the 12GB/512GB model.

Article Title: Jamie Dimon, whose own family is an example of American Dream, to Gen Z: You could be forgiven for giving up on American Dream, as if you look at ...
Article Text:
JPMorgan CEO Jamie Dimon

Jamie Dimon believes that the dream remains ‘totally achievable’

JPMorgan’s American Dream initiative

Capitalism under scrutiny

JPMorgan Chase CEO Jamie Dimon recently said that he understands why Gen Z feels the American Dream is slipping away. Between soaring away. Between soaring house prices, rising living costs, and the looming threat of AI reshaping the labour market, young Americans could be forgiven for doubting the historic ideal. A June AP-NORC poll found only one-fifth of adults aged 18 to 29 believe the American Dream is attainable. According to a report by Fortune, in an interview with Firing Line, Dimon pointed to his own family as proof of the Dream’s resilience. His grandparents immigrated from Greece without high school diplomas but instilled a strong sense of purpose in their children and grandchildren. That legacy helped Dimon rise to lead the largest bank in the U.S., a trajectory he says reflects the Dream’s enduring possibility.Speaking to PBS, Dimon argued the Dream remains “totally achievable” for most Americans, noting that the middle class has grown and wealth has increased overall. But he warned that the bottom 20% have seen stagnant incomes for decades, leaving them in struggling neighborhoods and underfunded schools. “For them, it’s slipping,” he said, adding that this inequality is fueling polarization and anger across society.Dimon highlighted JPMorgan’s American Dream Initiative, which focuses on six areas including small business support and skills-based training, as part of efforts to expand opportunity. He urged policymakers from both parties to acknowledge inequality and work on solutions, saying: “Whether you’re a Democrat or Republican, acknowledge the problem and then start to say, ‘How can you fix it?’”Dimon, who describes himself as a “patriotic, unwoke, capitalist CEO,” admitted capitalism has flaws but insisted it remains the best system available. He cautioned against conflating systemic imperfections with alternatives, noting that every system has “bad people.” His comments echo broader debates, with figures like Larry Fink of BlackRock warning that capitalism is fueling economic anxiety by failing too many people.
Article Summary: JPMorgan Chase CEO Jamie Dimon said he understands why Gen Z feels the American Dream is slipping away. A June AP-NORC poll found only one-fifth of adults aged 18 to 29 believe the Dream is attainable. Dimon highlighted JPMorgan’s American Dream Initiative, which focuses on six areas including small business support.

Article Title: OpenAI finally brings ChatGPT desktop app to Linux: Ubuntu, Debian and Fedora users get ChatGPT, Work and Codex in one place
Article Text:
File image: ChatGPT

Which Linux distros are supported, and what the app actually does

Linux users have spent years watching every major AI app land on Windows and macOS first, then waiting their turn. That wait just ended. OpenAI has released a dedicated ChatGPT desktop app for Linux, rolling it out worldwide on Tuesday in preview, bundling ChatGPT, ChatGPT Work and Codex into a single native experience.The company pitched it as closing the last gap in its desktop lineup. Linux was one of the most-requested platforms for the desktop app, OpenAI said, and the launch extends ChatGPT and Codex across every major desktop operating system. On paper it's a routine port. For a developer community that has been asking loudly, and for a long time, it reads differently.Support at launch covers Ubuntu 24.04 LTS and 26.04 LTS, Debian 13, and Fedora 43 and 44, across both x64 and ARM64, shipping as .deb and .rpm packages. That list looks thin next to the hundreds of distributions out there, but these are the bases for a long tail of downstream flavours, which should run the app fine as a result.What you get isn't just a chat window in a new wrapper. OpenAI positions the desktop app as a workspace: parallel projects, documents and spreadsheets opened and inspected in place, browser and computer-use workflows, scheduled tasks set up inside an existing chat, and Codex running alongside ChatGPT rather than in a separate tool.OpenAI isn't first here, though. Anthropic shipped a Claude desktop app for Linux roughly a month ago, and cast a wider net with it, supporting Ubuntu 22.04 or later and Debian 12 or later.The preview tag on OpenAI's build suggests the polish is still coming.
Article Summary: OpenAI releases ChatGPT desktop app for Linux on Tuesday. The company says Linux was one of the most-requested platforms for the app. Support covers Ubuntu 24.04 LTS and 26.04, as well as Debian 13 and Fedora 43 and 44.

Article Title: Everything announced at 'Made by Google 2026': Pixel 11 phones, Pixel Watch 5, and a lot more AI
Article Text:
Made by Google Event 2026

The Pixel 11 and the Pro are further apart than they've ever been

The Pixel 11 Pro Fold finally shuts flat

HiLight is the reason Google wants your phone face down

Tensor G6 is behind almost every number Google quoted

Magic Capture takes the photo you'd have missed

Gemini Intelligence wants to act before you ask

Pixel Watch 5 looks the same and isn't

But the best Pixel Watch 5 features aren't here yet

Pixel Buds Pro 2 just get a new colour

Four phones, a watch, two new chips and a health platform. A big day by any measure, and almost none of it something you can hold.The Pixel 11, Pixel 11 Pro, Pixel 11 Pro XL and Pixel 11 Pro Fold keep the camera bar and most of what surrounds it. New hardware comes down to three things: a Tensor G6, a rebuilt telephoto on the Pro, and a camera housing on the Fold reshaped so the phone finally shuts flat.The rest of the year went into software. Gemini Intelligence answering before you ask, Magic Capture taking the photo you'd have fumbled, and a Pixel Watch 5 that reads blood pressure trends without a cuff, then sits on the result for a month before saying anything. The Pixel Buds Pro 2, for their part, get a new colour and nothing else.There's one exception, and it's on the back of the Pixel 11 Pro. Google has put a ring of LEDs around the camera flash and called it HiLight. Every Nexus had one. The Pixel 2 had the last, and then always-on displays arrived and Google stopped bothering. Nine years on, the notification light is back, pointed at the wrong side of the phone on purpose.Here's everything Google announced, and the show itself runs later tonight, with Trevor Noah hosting and Stephen Curry, Alex Cooper and Peggy Gou along for the evening.The Pixel 11 and the Pro are further apart than they've ever beenThe two Pixels have less in common this year than they have in a while, though you wouldn't know it from the outside.The familiar camera bar keeps its shape, with the glass now running edge to edge into the frame rather than sitting on top, slimmest of all on the Pixel 11. The Pixel 11 got the cheerful colours and the Pro got the serious ones. Frost, Hibiscus, Pistachio and Obsidian on one side. Canyon, Olive, Fog and Matte Obsidian on the other, and that matte black is the first Google has offered on a Pro model.The Pixel 11 gets a 3,000-nit Actua panel behind Gorilla Glass Victus 2. The Pro pair gets Super Actua at 3,600 nits, which Google puts at 9 per cent brighter than last year and more than twice as scratch resistant, and is calling the toughest display it has shipped. Under the Pro models sits a vapour chamber to keep the chip from throttling during long camera sessions. All three are IP68.The cameras split the same way. A 48MP main on the Pixel 11, a 50MP main and a rebuilt telephoto on the Pro pair, and a gap in reach between the two that has never been wider. More on that below.Memory is the more consequential split, and it comes with a catch. The Pixel 11 starts at 256GB with 12GB of RAM, the highest floor a base Pixel has had. That isn't generosity. Gemini Intelligence won't run on less, so the floor had to move. The Pro pair climbs to 16GB and 512GB.Charging won't sell anybody a phone. It's still the upgrade you'll notice most often. All three clear 30 hours on Adaptive Battery, and half an hour on a cable takes the Pro XL to 75 per cent and the other two to 55. A new Extreme Charging Mode redirects the phone's whole performance budget into the battery for when you're in a rush.Pixelsnap magnets are built into the phones now instead of the case, worth up to 29 per cent faster wireless charging on the Pixel 11 Pro, 25 on the Pixel 11 and 17 on the Pro XL. A Clear Case, a silicone case and a Ring Stand go with them.The Pixel 11 is Rs 89,999, the Pixel 11 Pro is Rs 1,19,999 and the Pro XL is Rs 1,34,999. Buy either Pro and six months of Google AI Pro comes with it, which Google values at Rs 11,700.The camera housing on the Fold is now a dual pill instead of a block, and Google was oddly upfront about why. It was the thing stopping the phone from closing flush.That fix sits alongside a millimetre off the thickness, roughly a tenth off the weight, a new hinge, a soft-touch composite back, an IP68 rating, and a body Google's own testing puts at three times stronger than last year's.Both screens gain 20 per cent in brightness, and the outer one moves to Super Actua for the first time, which should matter more than the spec suggests given how much foldable time goes to the cover screen. Inside is an 8-inch Super Actua Flex panel.The camera is a 48MP main drawing 56 per cent more light than the Pixel 10 Pro Fold's, with a telephoto and 30x Super Zoom. Three features make use of the hinge itself. Made You Look plays animations on the outer screen while you frame, aimed at anyone who has tried to photograph a four-year-old. Dual Screen Preview lets your subject watch themselves pose. Rear Camera Selfie has you unfold the phone, frame yourself on the cover display and shoot with the main sensor rather than a front camera.Multitasking gets Split Screen, floating app Bubbles capped at five, drag and drop between apps, and a tabletop mode. There's 16GB of RAM, over 24 hours of battery and 50 per cent charge in half an hour. It costs Rs 1,86,999 with 512GB.The light sits in the camera bar where the flash normally goes, and it does nothing at all while the phone is face up.Two uses are there for now. The first is calls from specific contacts, each assigned its own colour, and because it works across both Phone by Google and WhatsApp, that colour holds whichever app the call arrives through. Set the phone down and Flip to Shhh silences it, while HiLight keeps a channel open for the handful of people you've picked out.The second is Gemini. The lights pulse through listening, thinking and answering, so a hands-free question doesn't end with you turning the phone over to see whether anything happened. Minor on paper, but it removes the main reason people feel self-conscious talking to an assistant in public.What Google hasn't said is whether HiLight handles ordinary app notifications, which is what the old Nexus light did best and what Nothing has built an entire design language around. It's the obvious third use, and probably the one that decides whether this is a feature or a flourish.HiLight is exclusive to the Pixel 11 Pro and Pro XL.Up to 20 per cent more power efficient than the G5. Browsing 25 per cent faster, apps loading 15 per cent quicker. Perfectly respectable figures, and not the ones anybody will remember this chip for.That job goes to the TPU, which gains 50 per cent more compute and funds Instant Night Sight, Magic Capture and the on-device Gemini work that used to need a round trip to a server. Google says the silicon was co-designed alongside DeepMind's model teams, which is how Gemini Nano ends up running faster and better than it did on the Pixel 10. The image signal processor was rebuilt too, and that's the less glamorous half of why the camera got quicker.Next to it sits a new security chip. Titan M3 brings post-quantum cryptography to the Pixel, guarding against decryption capabilities that don't exist yet and are widely expected to, and it carries the same Common Criteria certification used for SIM cards and bank cards.The everyday protections are easier to picture. Call Screen still answers unknown numbers and reports who's calling and why, and Scam Detection listens for the conversational patterns scammers use and warns you mid-call.Magic Capture is Google's replacement for burst mode, and it works from a fairly honest premise, which is that most people are worse at timing a shutter than they think.One swipe in the camera app opens it. From there it records video and pulls high-quality stills out of that video at the same time, cropping and unblurring them without being asked. You tap once and the timing stops being your problem. If any single feature from this event ends up in daily use, it's likely this one.Underneath it, the hardware moved too, and Google spent most of that budget on zoom. The Pro telephoto has been rebuilt around a sensor taking in 32 per cent more light and now reaches 120x, the longest Google has offered. More useful in practice is the new 50MP main on a 1/1.3-inch sensor with 2x optical quality, covering the 1x to 3x range where most photographs get taken. The Pixel 11 and the Fold share a 48MP main with 30x Super Zoom.Camera Looks lets you build and save your own film styles for HDR+ shots. Google has tied it firmly to Real Tone, insisting a heavily stylised look still has to render skin tones properly, which is a promise worth testing.Instant Night Sight cuts low-light capture time by up to 4.5 times on the Pro. The complaint about Night Sight was never the photograph it produced. It was how long you had to hold still for it.Video gets Pro Stable Video up to 8K through Video Boost, plus a new Creator tab with trimming and reordering tools, a Teleprompter, improved Speech Enhancement and clips that save themselves into project albums.A friend texts asking whether you're free, and your calendar surfaces on its own. Someone sends a restaurant, and the phone has it open and ready to book.That's the promise. Whether it lands as useful or exhausting comes down to how often it guesses right, and Google is keen to point out that you decide what data feeds it and can change that at any point.Two quieter changes look more dependable. Voice-to-text now strips filler words on its own, so the ums go and what you said arrives formatted. Writing help reads what's on screen and shapes replies towards how you write rather than towards a generic corporate register.Live Translate has been extended to video, podcasts and voice notes as they play, and Circle to Search has moved into the Pixel Camera, so you can identify an object, zoom into something far away or translate a sign without leaving the viewfinder.This is also the reason the Pixel 11's memory floor moved.Google kept the design, which was the easiest call it had to make all morning. The domed Actua 360 display and the pebble case both return, now in Obsidian, Fog, Olive and Canyon, with Olive on an all-new Satin Pyrite casing and Canyon exclusive to the 41mm.The rest of it changed. Qualcomm's Snapdragon W5 Gen 2 Accelerated runs Wear OS 7 at what Google calls 20 per cent faster than the Pixel Watch 4, with 64GB of storage. The screen peaks at 3,000 nits, and satellite SOS, ultra-wideband, dual-frequency GPS and 5 ATM water resistance are all included.The 45mm is rated for 40 hours with the always-on display and the 41mm for 30, though whether anyone wears this to bed comes down to charging: 15 minutes on the dock buys 15 hours.Watch faces get motion for the first time through a design called Weave, alongside a Chronograph option and the ability to generate a face from a written prompt. A Stephen Curry special edition stays in the US. Pricing starts at Rs 42,900.Everything new about this watch arrives in September, which is an unusual thing for a launch to concede.Health Guardian is the new umbrella over the watch's alerts and trend reports, and two of those reports are doing the heavy lifting. Blood Pressure Trends reads the shape of your pulse wave and how fast it travels beneath your skin, then works out whether your pressure has been running high across a full calendar month. Insulin Resistance Trends does something comparable for metabolic health, weaving heart rhythm, sleep quality and daily movement into an estimate of how hard your body is working to clear glucose. No blood, no cuff, no fasting, no appointment.Each reports once, on the first of the month, and that restraint is the entire design. Blood pressure moves around all day, and a daily number would hand you anxiety and nothing to do with it.The science isn't thin. Google trained the blood pressure model on billions of minutes of data from more than half a million people and tested it against 24-hour ambulatory monitoring, the clinical gold standard, with the research peer-reviewed in Nature.The caveats are stated just as plainly. Neither feature diagnoses anything, neither screens for hypertension or diabetes, neither should inform a decision about medication, and neither is meant for anyone pregnant. Both land on the Pixel Watch 3, 4 and 5 and on Fitbit Air, alongside Sleep Breathing Quality, which tracks how blood oxygen shifts overnight. Loss of pulse detection carries over, and breathing emergency detection stays limited to certain EU markets.The fitness work is on the same September clock. A Readiness Score tells you before a session whether to push or recover, strength and HIIT circuits can be built in the Google Health app and pushed to the wrist with audio and visual cues through every set and rest, over 50 exercise types are tracked, and a new Key Metrics view handles the review afterwards.Sleep gets Bedtime Automations, Smart Wake alarms and a rebuilt Morning Brief. Sitting above all of it is Google Health Coach, built with Gemini and locked behind Google Health Premium, which writes training plans that adapt to you and folds in Cycle Health. Three months come free with the watch, and it's bundled into Google AI Pro and AI Ultra.No new earbuds this year. The Pixel Buds Pro 2 pick up an Olive finish matching the Pixel 11 Pro and the Satin Pyrite casing on the Pixel Watch 5, and that's the whole update.Everything else carries over from 2024. The Tensor A1 chip, Silent Seal 2.0 noise cancellation, 11mm drivers, an IP54 rating, and roughly eight hours of listening with ANC switched on, or about 30 with the case.
Article Summary: The Pixel 11 and the Pro are further apart than they've ever been. The Pixel Buds Pro 2, for their part, get a new colour and nothing else. A new Extreme Charging Mode redirects the phone's whole performance budget into the battery for when you're in a rush.
