Google Pixel 11 series has been launched. The company has officially taken the wraps off its next-generation Pixel lineup at its “Made by Google” hardware event, bringing three new phones: the Google Pixel 11, Google Pixel 11 Pro and Google Pixel 11 Pro XL, with a new in-house chip, a powerful security setup and a fresh round of AI features built around Gemini. The company has also launched the Google Pixel 11 Pro Fold, Google Pixel Watch 5 (in two sizes), a new colour of the Google Pixel Bunds Pro 2 and a bunch of accessories, including PixelSnap Ring Stand and PixelSnap charger with stand. Here's a complete breakdown of what is new and what it will cost you in India.The Google Pixel 11 starts at Rs 89,999 for the base 256GB model that comes with 12GB RAM. The Pixel 11 Pro price in India starts at Rs 1,19,999 for the base 256GB and the Pixel 11 Pro XL price in India starts at Rs 1,34,999. This means that the Pixel 11 series gets a Rs 10,000 price hike across models.Pre-orders for the series are now open through Google's own store as well as partner retailers with devices going on sale fromColour options also differ across the lineup: the Google Pixel Pro and Google Pixel Pro XL come in Canyon, Olive, Fog and a matte Obsidian finish, while the standard Google Pixel 11 gets its own palette of Frost, Pistachio, Hibiscus and Obsidian.All three phones stick with Google’s familiar Pixel design language, but the Pro models get a notably brighter, sharper screen. The Pixel 11 Pro comes with a 6.3-inch Super Actua display, while the Pro XL steps up to a larger 6.8-inch panel with both offering adaptive refresh rate that scales between 1Hz and 120Hz. The standard Pixel 11 gets a slightly smaller Actua display with a 60-120Hz range instead.Peak brightness on the Pro models can hit up to 3,600 nits, while the standard Pixel 11 tops out at 3,000 nits. All three models use Corning's Gorilla Glass Victus 2 for protection, with the Pro models adding an anti-scratch shield on top. One of the most highlighting changes in the phones is HiLight – an array of ambient LED lights built around the camera’s flash to give you light-based communications on the back of the phone.When your phone is face down, HiLight gently glows to give you a visual cue to pick up your phone, or stay in the moment.When it comes to performance and security, powering the entire lineup is Google’s new Tensor G6 chip, paired with a Titan M3 security coprocessor across all three models. Google is pitching this as a meaningful jump in on-device security, with a multi-layered setup that includes quantum-safe secure boot built directly into the hardware.Google Pixel phones have led the cameras department when it comes to point-and-shoot photography. The Google Pixel 11 Pro and Google Pixel 11 Pro XL share an identical camera setup: a 50MP wide lens, a 48MP ultrawide camera with macro focus, and a 48MP telephoto lens offering 5x optical zoom and up to 120x Pro Zoom. The standard Pixel 11 gets a slightly toned-down system: a 48MP wide camera, a 13MP ultrawide lens, and a 10.8MP telephoto sensor capped at 30x Super Zoom.On the front, the Pro models get a 42MP selfie camera, compared to 10.5MP on the standard Pixel 11. All three models support Google's usual suite of computational photography tools, including Night Sight, Astrophotography, Magic Eraser, Best Take, and the newer Edit with Ask Photos feature, which lets you make edits using natural-language prompts.Talking about battery, charging and durability, all three phones promise over 30 hours of battery life, backed by battery capacities ranging from 4,850mAh on the Pixel 11 Pro to up to 5,115mAh on the larger Google Pixel 11 Pro XL. All three also support Pixelsnap wireless charging at up to 25W, and come with an IP68 rating for dust and water resistance.Coming to the AI features and software, every model in the lineup ships with Gemini Intelligence built in, powered by Google's on-device Gemini Nano model. That includes access to Gemini Live for real-time conversational AI, along with Magic Cue, a feature designed to proactively surface relevant information based on what's happening on your screen. Google is also backing the lineup with a lengthy software commitment with all three phones are promised seven years of OS updates, security patches and Pixel Drop feature updates, running on Android 17 out of the box.
Article Summary: Google Pixel 11, Google Pixel 11 Pro and Google Pixel Pro XL have been launched in India. Pre-orders for the Pixel 11 series are open through Google's own as well as partner retailers with devices going on sale from August 20. The company has officially taken the wraps off its next-generation Pixel lineup at its “Made by Google’s” hardware event.

Article Title: Months after Michael Dell and his wife Susan Dell's $6.25 billion donation, Department of Treasury announces new 'paycheck rules' for Trump Accounts
Article Text:
Representative Image

US Treasury proposes new Trump Accounts paycheck rules

“Trump Accounts are giving American families a new way to build wealth from day one,”

“Today, Treasury is publishing guidance that will help families grow Trump Accounts by allowing employers to contribute up to $2,500 tax-free each year for employees’ dependents and giving employees the option to contribute pre-tax dollars directly to those accounts,”

Who can contribute to Trump Accounts

Employer participation in Trump Accounts

“We saw early adoptions, and I think many more are considering it, and this guidance is going to help,”

The US Treasury Department and Internal Revenue Service (IRS) have proposed new rules for Trump Accounts. These new rules will allow employers and employees to contribute to Trump Accounts through workplace payroll systems. The latest rules come months after Dell Technologies founder and CEO Michael Dell and his wife Susan Dell pledged $6.25 billion to help fund the child savings initiative. Sharing the new rules, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said the guidance will allow employers to contribute up to $2,500 tax-free each year for employees' dependent children and will allow workers to make pre-tax paycheck contributions directly into the accounts.In December 2025, Michael Dell revealed that the Michael and Susan Dell Foundation plans to commit $6.25 billion to the savings program, formerly known as Trump Accounts and later renamed Invest America accounts. The donation is intended to provide $250 to the accounts of 25 million American children when the program begins, exceeding the foundation's total charitable giving over its previous 26 years.The Treasury Department and IRS released the proposed regulations this week outlining how employers can establish and fund Trump Accounts, also known as 530A accounts.Under the proposal, qualifying employer contributions would be excluded from an employee's gross income, and employers could also allow workers to fund their dependent children's accounts through pre-tax payroll deductions.Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said in a statement.Bessent added.The proposal is now open for public comment, with a hearing scheduled for October before the regulations can be finalised.Trump Accounts are available to any US child under 18 with a Social Security number. Children born between 2025 and 2028 are eligible for a one-time $1,000 Treasury deposit under a pilot programme designed to encourage long-term savings. According to Bessent, about 7 million children have already been enrolled.Once an account is opened, parents, guardians, grandparents and other contributors can deposit up to $5,000 annually until the year before the child turns 18. Within that limit, employers may contribute up to $2,500 per employee each year.The US Treasury said more than 50 companies have already committed to contributing to Trump Accounts for their employees, with some employers also planning to match the government's $1,000 seed contribution.Melissa Elbert, partner of wealth solutions at retirement benefits consultant Aon, said the latest guidance provides employers with greater clarity on the administrative and compliance framework for implementing the programme.Elbert said.Earlier this year, a Mercer survey of nearly 350 US employers found that only about 4% expected to introduce Trump Account contribution programmes in 2026 or 2027, while about two-thirds had already decided against participating. Others remained undecided before the Treasury released its proposed rules.
Article Summary: US Treasury proposes new Trump Accounts paycheck rules. New rules will allow employers to contribute up to $2,500 tax-free each year for employees’ dependents and give employees the option to contribute pre-tax dollars directly to those accounts. The proposal is now open for public comment.

Article Title: Quote of the day by Tim Cook: “The sidelines are not where you want to live your life. The world needs you in the arena”
Article Text:
Apple CEO Tim Cook

Quote of the day by Tim Cook

“The sidelines are not where you want to live your life. The world needs you in the arena.”

Tim Cook’s message to young people

Cook’s call to challenge the status quo

The leadership lesson behind Cook’s words

Why the quote remains relevant

Tim Cook has often spoken about the importance of taking action, accepting responsibility and using one’s abilities to make a meaningful difference. One of his most memorable messages came during his 2015 commencement address at George Washington University, where he urged graduates not to remain passive observers when the world faces problems that need solving. Cook told students that critics and cynics would always exist, but argued that simply watching from the sidelines was not enough. Instead, he encouraged them to step forward, take risks and contribute to progress. His message continues to resonate with students, professionals and entrepreneurs who may find themselves hesitating before taking the next important step in their lives. Cook's message ultimately centres on the idea that meaningful change requires participation, not simply criticism from a distance. By choosing to act despite uncertainty or opposition, individuals can turn their abilities and convictions into something that has a tangible impact.Tim Cook delivered these words during his commencement address to George Washington University’s Class of 2015 on May 17, 2015. Speaking on the National Mall, Cook encouraged graduates to think beyond their individual careers and consider how they could contribute to solving some of the world’s biggest problems.He pointed to issues including injustice, persecution and diseases that still needed cures, telling the graduates that the world needed their energy, passion and impatience with progress.Cook’s message was essentially a call to action. The “sidelines” represent a passive position where people watch events unfold, criticise decisions or wait for someone else to take responsibility. The “arena”, by contrast, represents active participation. Cook wanted graduates to understand that meaningful change requires people who are willing to step forward, face difficult problems and accept the possibility of failure. His argument was that simply identifying problems is not enough. People also need to be willing to become part of the effort to solve them.The message was particularly significant because Cook acknowledged that people who take action will inevitably face criticism. He told graduates that there would always be “cynics and critics on the sidelines” trying to tear people down. However, he also warned about another kind of passivity: people with good intentions who make no contribution at all. By drawing this distinction, Cook suggested that good intentions alone are insufficient. What matters is the willingness to turn those beliefs into action.Cook’s speech was not simply about finding a successful career. He encouraged graduates to think about the kind of impact they wanted to have on the world. He urged them to identify their values and use those values as a guide when making professional and personal decisions. George Washington University described his message as an encouragement to combine moral beliefs with vocational aspirations and to have the courage to challenge existing ideas.Cook also connected his message to his own experiences. During the speech, he recalled his first visit to Washington in 1977 as a teenager from Alabama. He discussed his discomfort with then-Governor George Wallace, whose segregationist politics conflicted with Cook’s own values. The story helped establish one of the central ideas of his speech: people should not simply accept the circumstances around them when those circumstances conflict with what they believe is right.The quote also carries a lesson about risk. People can remain on the sidelines because taking action brings the possibility of criticism, mistakes or failure. It can feel safer to observe what others are doing, point out their mistakes and wait until the outcome is clear before getting involved. Cook’s message challenges that approach. He argued that progress requires people who are willing to accept uncertainty and participate even when success is not guaranteed.His words are particularly relevant to people at the beginning of their careers. A student may hesitate to apply for an ambitious role, an employee may avoid proposing an unconventional idea, and an entrepreneur may postpone starting a business because of the possibility of failure. Cook’s message suggests that waiting indefinitely for perfect certainty can itself become a barrier. Entering the “arena” means accepting that mistakes are possible while still deciding that participation is worthwhile.Another important element of the speech was Cook’s emphasis on challenging established ideas. He argued that great progress is possible regardless of the field a person chooses. For him, innovation was not limited to technology or business. It could also involve confronting injustice, improving society or finding solutions to problems that had remained unresolved for years.This idea reflects a broader theme in Cook’s leadership philosophy. He has frequently spoken about values and the responsibility of individuals and organisations to use their influence constructively. At George Washington University, he told graduates that their values could serve as a “North Star” and warned that a career without a sense of purpose could become little more than a job.Cook’s message extends beyond students and applies to leadership, careers and everyday decisions. Taking responsibility means moving from discussing what should change to asking what contribution you can make yourself. A person does not need to hold a powerful position to make a difference. They can begin by challenging an unfair practice, supporting an important cause, developing a useful idea or simply refusing to remain silent when action is needed.The quote also highlights the difference between criticism and contribution. It is easy to identify what is wrong with someone else’s work or with a difficult situation. It is much harder to step forward and attempt to improve it. Cook’s “arena” metaphor therefore places responsibility on the individual. If a problem matters enough to criticise, it may also matter enough to become involved in solving.More than a decade after Cook delivered the speech, the message remains relevant because the challenge he described is not limited to one generation. Every generation faces problems that require people willing to participate rather than simply observe. Technology, business, education, climate change, inequality and public health all require ideas as well as action.Cook ended his address with an even stronger message to the graduates: “History rarely yields to one person, but think and never forget what happens when it does.” He then told them, “That can be you. That should be you. That must be you.”At its core, his quote is a reminder that meaningful progress rarely comes from people who spend their lives watching from a distance. It comes from those willing to enter the arena, accept uncertainty and use their energy to make something better. For anyone standing at a crossroads, Cook’s message offers a simple challenge: do not just watch the world change. Find a way to become part of that change.
Article Summary: Tim Cook delivered these words during his commencement address to George Washington University’s Class of 2015 on May 17, 2015. His message was essentially a call to action. Cook wanted graduates to understand that meaningful change requires people who are willing to step forward, face difficult problems and accept the possibility of failure.

Article Title: Scientist are not happy with Spacex, Amazon and other companies’ plan to build millions of 'data centers’ in Space; raise 'Night Sky' warning
Article Text:
The SpaceX logo is displayed on a building, May 26, 2020, at the Kennedy Space Center in Cape Canaveral, Fla. (Photo: AP )

What makes scientists unhappy with Space datacenters

As tech giants and aerospace startups race to launch space-based data centers, scientists are warning that hundreds of thousands of new satellites could transform Earth into a ringed planet, drastically escalating light pollution and disrupting the night sky. In a new paper titled "Rings in the Sky," University of Regina astronomy professor Samantha Lawler, alongside Aaron Boley of the University of British Columbia and Hanno Rein of the University of Toronto, warned about the severe visual and environmental impact of proposed orbital data center mega-constellations."What would the sky look like if companies actually launched the tens of thousands up to one million "AI data center" satellites that they have asked for? Well, the short answer is, horrifying. The long answer is... this paper!" Lawler wrote in a social media post highlighting the research. He wrote in another post, "Here's the future that the techbros want. Earth as a ringed planet."The warning comes as companies—including SpaceX, Blue Origin, and startups such as Starcloud and Cowboy Space propose plans that could collectively send up to 1.2 million satellites into orbit. The projected figure dwarfs the roughly 16,000 active satellites currently orbiting Earth by more than 75 times, raising severe concerns regarding space debris, orbital congestion, collision risks, and optical interference for ground-based astronomy.SpaceX has touted its proposed "Starmind" data center constellation as an eco-friendly alternative to ground facilities, arguing that harvesting continuous solar energy in orbit reduces carbon footprints and relieves pressure on terrestrial power grids. Other industry players are similarly targeting space-based solar power to fuel high-performance GPUs equipped with specialized liquid-cooling systems.However, scientists point out that to continuously harvest solar energy, these orbiting data centers must occupy specific "sun-synchronous" orbits along the polar terminator—the moving line that divides day and night on Earth.By aligning along this line, entire constellations can perpetually face the sun while circling the globe over the poles. According to the researchers, this specific trajectory will inevitably create dense, artificial ring structures around the planet.“These systems would produce large ring structures with each ring passing through the sky twice a day. The largest impacts are expected to occur during winter, where ring structures could be seen sweeping through otherwise dark skies,” the authors wrote in their paper. Because the data centers require massive solar arrays and heavy hardware, their physical size will make them exceptionally reflective.Simulations and visual models created by Lawler demonstrate that constellations from SpaceX, Blue Origin, and Cowboy Space would be prominently visible from the ground, particularly during twilight hours at 6 p.m. and again around 3 a.m. Blue Origin’s proposed "Sunrise" constellation, which spans two rings, would remain almost constantly visible during night hours in northern polar regions.The findings echo growing concerns across the scientific community regarding the rapid commercialization of Low Earth Orbit. Speaking to Space.com last month, Hugh Lewis, a professor of astronautics and space debris expert at the University of Birmingham, offered a stark assessment of the proposed constellations: “The impact on the night sky would be absolutely catastrophic."
Article Summary: Scientists warn that hundreds of thousands of new satellites could transform Earth into a ringed planet. Tech giants and aerospace startups race to launch space-based data centers. Researchers warn of severe visual and environmental impact of proposed orbital data center mega-constellations.

Article Title: Google's ex-chief scientist Jeff Dean shares last few hours at Google: Tears, lots of emotional chat, explosion of sad emojis and one minute of…
Article Text:
Jeff Dean, Google's 30th employee and chief scientist, is leaving after 27 years to lead AI startup Discovery Loop.

Jeff Dean's Google farewell party was booked for 300 and 1,500 people showed up

Why Jeff Dean stayed up till 2:30 AM answering Google chat messages

Unemployed for exactly one minute, then Jeff Dean became the co-founder of Discovery Loop

Jeff Dean spent his final night as a Google employee doing what most departing executives hand off to an auto-reply. He sat up until 2:30 in the morning answering 400 goodbye messages one by one, because his corporate account was about to expire and take every one of them with it.Speaking at the KDD Conference in Jeju, South Korea, Google's former chief scientist put up a slide with an hour-by-hour timeline of his last two days at the company he joined in 1999 as employee number 30. He later posted it on X with an apology attached: anyone who messaged him after Thursday afternoon never got a reply, because by then the laptop was shut for good.The timeline starts early last Wednesday, when roughly 12 people at Google knew Dean was going. At 8:30 AM he told 139 close colleagues on a video call, and his own summary of it is the most-quoted line of the week: tears, explosions of heart and sad face emojis, lots of chats running on the side of the meeting. If 139 close colleagues sounds implausible, consider that Dean managed about 4,400 people across Google Research and AI, a number that surfaced in Discovery Loop's pitch deck.Half an hour later, two things went out at once: the public announcement of Discovery Loop and the internal farewell email, the one listing MapReduce and BigTable alongside Monterey bike rides and 18 desk moves.By 2:30 PM there was a party. Google had booked a cafe space that holds about 300. Around 1,500 people came.Then Dean, who keeps a group run called "Run or Else…" going, went to a 7 PM yoga session and played a soccer league game at 8:30. He got home at 10:30 PM to those 400 messages.The urgency was technical, not sentimental. Internal chats lived on the corporate account, and the corporate account was expiring. Everything in that inbox would be gone the next day, so he answered all 400 and went to sleep at 2:30 AM. Four hours later he woke to 250 more, plus 500 replies to the farewell email that had CC'd his personal Gmail. At least those won't disappear in eight hours, he noted on the slide.Thursday was a losing race. By 5:20 PM he had cleared nearly every corporate message and they were still arriving. He closed the laptop anyway.At 11:59:59 PM, the slide reads: Unemployed. One second past midnight on Friday, it reads co-founder of Discovery Loop, alongside Sanjay Ghemawat, Oriol Vinyals and Quoc Le. The startup is a public benefit corporation backed by Alphabet, Radical Ventures and Khosla Ventures, aiming to automate the experimental loop itself and run thousands of AI-designed experiments in parallel across machine learning, chip design and drug discovery. Alphabet is supplying compute for the first year.The exit lands inside a wider AI reshuffle at Google, with Demis Hassabis moving out of the Google DeepMind CEO role into a chairman post and CTO Koray Kavukcuoglu elevated to SVP. Dean followed the KDD slide with a photo of his surrendered badge and sticker-covered Chromebook, captioned "Turned it in…". That post has crossed 2.8 million views.
Article Summary: Jeff Dean, Google's 30th employee and chief scientist, is leaving after 27 years to lead AI startup Discovery Loop. Dean spent his final night as a Google employee doing what most departing executives hand off to an auto-reply. He sat up until 2:30 in the morning answering 400 goodbye messages one by one.

Article Title: Apple's 20th-anniversary iPhone isn't dead, but it just lost some glass
Article Text:
Apple's 20th-anniversary iPhone is still on for 2027, but with less glass than first rumoured.

What actually got cancelled was the more ambitious version

The most talked-about iPhone of 2027 is still happening, just not in the form the rumour mill had settled on. Bloomberg reports that Apple is going ahead with a glass-centric redesign for the iPhone's 20th anniversary next year, with the new look reserved for the Pro models. Glass runs across the front and back and curves into the sides, broken up by a metal band through the middle. The two devices are known internally as V73 and V74.That puts Bloomberg at odds with Jefferies analyst Edison Lee, who told clients earlier this week that supply chain checks showed the all-glass iPhone had been canned over poor yields. Lee called it a major setback for Apple's push into pricier iPhones at a time when memory costs are climbing, and downgraded the stock on the back of it. Bloomberg's sources say the product roadmap hasn't changed at all.Apple's design studio had pushed for a far more aggressive concept that swapped out the metal for even more glass. That one died early. Engineers ran into trouble joining the glass panels together, and the design fell apart once the question turned to manufacturing it in the millions. So the anniversary phone survives as an evolution of the idea rather than the purist version.Timing supports Bloomberg's account. Apple typically locks an iPhone design roughly a year before its September reveal, which means the 2027 phones are already deep in testing.Before any of that, there's next month. Apple is expected to show a foldable iPhone, the biggest change to the product's shape yet, alongside the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max with camera upgrades and a new dark red finish. The base iPhone 18, the 18e and a second-generation iPhone Air follow in spring. All of it lands on John Ternus, who becomes CEO on September 1.
Article Summary: Apple's 20th-anniversary iPhone is still on for 2027, but with less glass than first rumoured. That one died early. Engineers ran into trouble joining the glass panels together. So the anniversary phone survives as an evolution of the idea rather than the purist version.

Article Title: Subco CEO sends 'urgent message' to Australian Police after two undersea cables damaged, hints at suspicious activity; read message
Article Text:
Image source: Linkedin/Bevan Slattery

What are shunt faults

Subco CEO flags 'suspicious' vessel activity near cable faults

Australian Federal Police confirms investigation

Australia's Federal Police (AFP) is investigating after two undersea communication cables owned by Subco reported faults within minutes of each other. The fault has prompted the company's founder and CEO Bevan Slattery to urge authorities to launch an urgent probe. Slattery said the two cables developed "shunt faults" in close proximity inside a federally protected submarine cable zone off Perth, while what he described as "suspicious/coincidental" activity from a vessel was also recorded near the location at around the same time. The AFP confirmed it had received a report of a crime and is assessing the information.A shunt fault occurs when the insulation around a conductor is damaged, allowing unintended contact with another conductor or the ground, effectively creating a short circuit. Slattery also shared the track of a marine vessel that was allegedly operating near the approximate location of the cable faults when they were detected. However, no evidence has yet linked the vessel to the incident.In a LinkedIn post, Slattery said the Indigo-West cable, which connects Perth to Indonesia and Singapore, and the Indigo-Central cable, which connects Victoria, Tasmania and New South Wales, both reported shunt faults one after another."Earlier tonight: Shunt faults on two systems (Indigo West and Indigo Central) straight after each other and in close proximity to each other. Remarkably this also happened in the Submarine Cable Protection Zone off Perth Australia," he wrote.He added that there was "some suspicious/coincidental activity from a vessel near the location and timing of the shunts occurring."Calling the incident concerning, Slattery said submarine cables are "the digital lifeblood of our nation" and urged the Australian Federal Police to investigate the matter urgently. He also noted that this could become the second such incident inside a federally declared cable protection zone if sabotage is confirmed.Here's what he wrote"Earlier tonight: Shunt faults on two systems (Indigo West and Indigo Central) straight after each other and in close proximity to each other. Remarkably this also happened in the Submarine Cable Protection Zone off Perth Australia.Coincidently some suspicious/coincidental activity from a vessel near the location and timing of the shunts occurring.This is a concerning development. Partially because submarine cables are the digital lifeblood of our nation, but also because this this could very well turn out to be the second such incidence in a Federally declared cable protection zone.This maybe a coincidence, but it’s important for the Australian Federal Police to investigate the issue urgently."The AFP confirmed that it had received a report related to the incident. "The AFP has received a report of crime in relation to this matter," the agency said in a statement, adding that the report is currently being assessed and further comments will be made when appropriate.So far, authorities have not confirmed whether the cables were intentionally damaged.
Article Summary: Two undersea communication cables owned by Subco reported faults within minutes of each other. The fault has prompted the company's founder and CEO Bevan Slattery to urge authorities to launch an urgent probe. Slattery said the two cables developed "shunt faults" in close proximity inside a federally protected submarine cable zone off Perth. The AFP confirmed it had received a report of a crime and is assessing the information.

Article Title: Conservation grants, millions to local schools and more: How Meta managed data center just miles away from Kevin O’Leary’s ‘failed dream project’
Article Text:
Representative Image

Meta's Eagle Mountain data center and early community outreach

"I think we did set some clear expectations in the beginning,"

"Man,"

"these guys really do what they say."

Kevin O'Leary's Project Stratos faces community backlash

"We really scr*wed this up,"

"We have not communicated what we do."

Political fallout in Box Elder County

"We here in the West have a history of overcoming hardships and challenges," she said, adding, "I think [O'Leary] just set himself up for a really big fight [in Box Elder County]."

What comes next for the Utah data center

"I got a lot of work ahead of me,"

"If I've said anything that offends you, yes, I apologize. If I've done anything that you think has been unfair, I apologize. But I also, with that, would say I want you to lend an open ear to what I'm going to show you in the months ahead."

Facebook-parent Meta has been able to do something that Kevin O'Leary has failed to do: win over the local community around its Utah data center. Meta secured approval and support from residents in Eagle Mountain, while O'Leary's Project Stratos in Box Elder County, which is just miles away from the Mark Zuckerberg-led social media giant’s data center has faced sustained backlash since its ‘quiet’ approval in May.Both projects sit on opposite ends of the Great Salt Lake, but the outcomes have diverged sharply. Meta's Eagle Mountain facility, which opened in 2021, is now held up by locals and industry observers as an example of proper community engagement. O'Leary's proposal, by contrast, has become a cautionary tale as developers race to build data centers to meet AI-driven energy demand.Meta broke ground on its Eagle Mountain facility in 2018 and engaged city leaders well before construction began. Mayor Jared Gray told MS Now that the city reached agreements with Meta covering taxation and power usage ahead of time.Gray said.Since opening, Meta has provided conservation grants to 20 organisations across Eagle Mountain, according to Gray. The company has also invested millions of dollars in local schools, funding a hydroponic garden at the high school and providing laptops for every student there.Gray said, describing the town's view of the company,O'Leary's proposal has been shaped by limited outreach and shifting plans. He originally sought to acquire 40,000 acres, an area twice the size of Manhattan, before reducing the footprint by half following community pushback. The project is still expected to draw up to 9 gigawatts of power.Dr Robert Davies, associate professor of physics at Utah State University and a leading critic of the project, compared its power consumption to that of two states of Utah or three New York Cities. He said the resulting heat output could raise temperatures in the valley and speed up evaporation near the Great Salt Lake, which has already lost three-quarters of its volume over several decades.O'Leary acknowledged the communication failures directly.he told MS Now.The approval of Project Stratos carried political consequences almost immediately. Republican voters ousted several local officials who had supported the project in primaries the month after its approval, including the state Senate president.Mare Burningham, who received a Meta grant to study deer migration patterns in Eagle Mountain, described the region's resistance to outside development.O'Leary has since adopted a more conciliatory tone, despite ongoing litigation tied to the project. He told MS Now he still plans to submit permit applications, which would provide the information residents have been requesting.Three months after the project's initial approval, O'Leary's company has not released those plans or disclosed which entity will use the data capacity once built.he said.Meta operates 28 data centers across the US and has faced criticism elsewhere, from concerns over water quality in Georgia to questions about real estate deals in Louisiana. But in Eagle Mountain, the company is seen more as a cooperative presence, a contrast often drawn to the ongoing standoff in Box Elder County.
Article Summary: Meta secured approval and support from residents in Eagle Mountain, Utah. Kevin O'Leary's Project Stratos in Box Elder County has faced backlash since its 'quiet' approval in May. Both projects sit on opposite ends of the Great Salt Lake, but the outcomes have diverged sharply.

Article Title: Oracle layoffs: Company's '6 am layoff emails' may return in next few days, as Oracle plans…
Article Text:
Oracle layoffs 2026: Company plans fresh job cuts this month after shedding 21,000 roles in a year, as AI data centre spending mounts.

Oracle has already cut 21,000 job in a single fiscal year

Every job cut is buying Oracle a bit more room to keep building data centres

Oracle’s revenue is climbing, which is what makes these layoffs land badly

The March layoffs left 600 Oracle workers fighting over severance, RSUs and H-1B support

Oracle employees have been told, in effect, to keep an eye on their inboxes. The company has drawn up plans for a fresh round of job cuts this month, Business Insider reported, citing people familiar with the plans and an internal document. The cuts could reach double-digit percentages on some teams, and managers have already been asked to submit lists of affected employees.The deadline is what makes this urgent. Oracle wants payroll reduced by the time its second quarter begins on September 1, which is barely three weeks away. And anyone who was around on March 31 knows exactly what that can look like: emails from "Oracle Leadership" arriving at roughly 6 am local time, no HR call, no manager warning, and one line doing all the work—"we have made the decision to eliminate your role." System access was cut the same morning. Employees in the US, India, Canada and Mexico were affected. Oracle declined to comment on the new plans.This would not be a fresh start so much as a continuation. Oracle's headcount fell by 21,000, or about 13%, in the fiscal year that ended May 31, taking the company from 162,000 employees to roughly 141,000. Restructuring costs jumped to $1.8 billion from $374 million a year earlier.In its annual filing, Oracle was unusually direct about why, saying the adoption of AI across its operations has already resulted in workforce reductions and may continue to.The arithmetic behind the cuts is not subtle. Oracle spent $55.7 billion on infrastructure last fiscal year and burned $23.7 billion more cash than it took in. It raised $43 billion in debt and another $5 billion through stock sales, and expects to raise about $40 billion more this year. TD Cowen had estimated in January that trimming 20,000 to 30,000 roles could free up $8-10 billion in incremental free cash flow. That number now reads less like a forecast and more like a plan.Oracle is not a company in trouble on paper. Revenue rose 17% last fiscal year and its cloud infrastructure business grew 77%. Net income jumped 95% to $6.13 billion in a recent quarter, and CEO Clay Magouyrk has pointed to $553 billion in remaining performance obligations as proof that demand for AI compute is outrunning supply. The stock disagrees. Oracle shares are down about 26% this year, hit both by anxiety over its debt load and by a wider selloff in software, on fears AI will eat traditional enterprise tools. Chairman Larry Ellison has dismissed that second worry, telling analysts in March the "SaaSpocalypse" would be someone else's problem.The March cuts left a residue Oracle hasn't cleared. More than 600 former employees signed a letter on April 17 seeking higher severance, extended healthcare, H-1B support and stock acceleration. Oracle replied that it would handle concerns individually, not as a group. A survey of 272 laid-off workers found 62% were over 40 and 27% had restricted stock due to vest within 90 days—stock that vanished on the way out. In India, severance in the earlier round broadly followed the N+2 formula, with unvested RSUs forfeited.Whether the next batch of emails arrives at 6 am is, at this point, the only detail still unknown.
Article Summary: Oracle has drawn up plans for a fresh round of job cuts this month. The cuts could reach double-digit percentages on some teams. The deadline is what makes this urgent. Oracle wants payroll reduced by the time its second quarter begins on September 1, which is barely three weeks away.

Article Title: After Bill Gates' daughter Phoebe Gates' shopping app accused of taking credit for sales it didn't drive, report makes new claim on '24-hour-excuse'
Article Text:
Bill Gates' daughter Phoebe Gates knew about 'cookie stuffing', says report

Internal slack records detail ‘Auto Drop’ features

Code reviews suggest 'automatic refresh of tracking cookies'

Internal communications and software records at Phia, the personal shopping startup co-founded by Bill Gates daughter Phoebe Gates and Sophia Kianni, indicate that the founders were allegedly aware of software features designed to claim unauthorised sales commissions at least seven months before the company publicly blamed the practice on a sudden “software bug. ” Citing internal Slack messages and source code reviews, Bloomberg reports that the practice, which is known in the affiliate marketing industry as “cookie stuffing”, was active as early as December.The timeline contradicts a public statement issued by the company on July 8, which claimed leadership had only discovered the tracking behavior “within the last 24 hours”.Phia operates as a browser extension designed to help shoppers automatically find discount codes and compare prices at online checkout counters. In exchange, partner retailers pay the platform an affiliate commission when its software helps convert a sale.However, internal chats accessed by the publication reveal that Phia implemented automated features that injected its tracking cookies into a shopper’s checkout session without requiring any user interaction, such as clicking a deal link or applying a coupon code, the Bloomberg report says. By dropping tracking identifiers automatically, Phia claimed credit and commissions for transactions it did not drive, a practice that is strictly prohibited by commercial network contracts and partner agreements.The report further claims that Slack discussions from December show Gates enquiring about whether automated cookie insertion was active across partner sites. In one exchange, Gates asked developers to confirm that “auto pop for cookie drop is live on ALL sites w a coupon to confirm we are monetizing on all gmv [gross merchandise value].”Additional source code reviews showed secondary features, including a “passive trigger” that automatically refreshed tracking cookies every two hours on top retail sites, which essentially increased the likelihood that Phia would overwrite competing referral links and secure the payout.This alleged ‘unauthorised’ attribution strategy generated a substantial portion of the company's daily income. Following the deactivation of these features in early July, Phia’s average daily revenue dropped from approximately $80,000 to between $10,000 and $28,000, the report said.An internal analysis conducted by a company data scientist in July estimated that unauthorised cookie insertion accounted for roughly 51% of the total merchandise value Phia claimed credit for selling in June.A spokesperson for Phia disputed the internal revenue estimates, stating the preliminary analysis relied on an “incorrect methodology.” The company attributed the broader drop in daily income to its decision to pause wider monetisation tools during an internal review.
Article Summary: Bill Gates' daughter Phoebe Gates knew about 'cookie stuffing', says report. Internal slack records detail ‘Auto Drop’ features.Code reviews suggest 'automatic refresh of tracking cookies' Bloomberg reports that the practice, which is known in the affiliate marketing industry as “cookie stuffing”, was active as early as December.

Article Title: FDA clears hearing aid feature on Samsung Galaxy Buds
Article Text:
Samsung introduced the Personal Sound Amplification Product (PSAP) feature on Galaxy Buds+ in 2020

Samsung announced that its Galaxy Buds Hearing Aid feature has received US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) clearance, enabling compatible Galaxy Buds to serve as an over-the-counter (OTC) hearing aid, offering users 18 years and older a convenient solution for addressing perceived mild to moderate hearing loss. Users can also diagnose their hearing with the Galaxy Buds Hearing Test feature, which is registered as a Software as a Medical Device (SaMD) and provides medical-grade results.Commenting on the launch, Hon Pak, Senior Vice President and Head of the Digital Health Team for the Mobile eXperience (MX) Business at Samsung Electronics said “Hearing health is a vital component of our overall well-being, profoundly impacting how we communicate, connect with loved ones and engage with the world,” adding “With the latest clearance from the FDA, we are expanding access to hearing support and making proactive care effortless by integrating the Hearing Test and Hearing Aid functionality directly into the Galaxy Buds. ”Samsung introduced a Personal Sound Amplification Product (PSAP) feature on Galaxy Buds+ in 2020. The PSAP feature was clinically validated in 2021 as effective support for daily communication for those with hearing loss.To develop this new OTC solution, Samsung collaborated closely with the National Acoustic Laboratories (NAL) and Samsung Medical Center (SMC). The resulting technology is backed by robust clinical validation studies conducted at Vanderbilt University Medical Center, San Jose State University and the University of Memphis.Based on those results, the Hearing Aid feature amplifies the sounds users have difficulty hearing — such as high frequencies, surrounding whispers and distant voices — personalized to each user’s hearing profile.Samsung said the hearing aid also supports additional advanced features typically found in premium hearing aids, such as noise elimination and beamforming, which help focus sounds in front of the user and suppress background noise. The Hearing Aid and Hearing Test features will be available on Galaxy Buds 3 Pro and Galaxy Buds 4 Pro in the US and select approved markets in Q4 2026.
Article Summary: Samsung announced that its Galaxy Buds Hearing Aid feature has received US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) clearance. The feature will be available on Galaxy Bud's 3 Pro and 4 Pro in the US and select approved markets in Q4 2026. Samsung introduced a Personal Sound Amplification Product (PSAP) feature on Galaxy buds+ in 2020.

Article Title: Aluminium foil, stainless steel, parchment paper, and other things that are unsafe while cooking in microwave but can be used in an air fryer
Article Text:
AI-generated image for representation

Why the two appliances behave so differently

AI-generated image for representation

What you can safely put in an air fryer

Aluminium foil

Parchment and air fryer liners:

Ai-generated image for representation

Stainless steel and other ovenproof metals

Glass and ceramic:

Silicone moulds and small cast-iron cookware:

Where airflow, not just heat, becomes the deciding factor

Materials to keep out of either appliance

FAQs

Can I put aluminium foil in an air fryer?

Why is aluminium foil dangerous in a microwave?

Can stainless steel be used in an air fryer?

Can parchment paper go in an air fryer?

Can glass and ceramic dishes be used in an air fryer?

Can a microwave-safe container be used in an air fryer?

What should I check before using a vessel in an air fryer?

Putting metals in a microwave usually results in sparks. Placing the same piece of metal in an air fryer usually isn't a problem. The difference is not due to luck, but to the fundamental way the two appliances cook food.Safe materials to put in an air fryer include aluminium foil, stainless steel, oven-safe glass and ceramics, food-safe silicone, and small cast-iron pans. These metals pose a problem when placed in the microwave because they reflect microwave radiation, which can cause sparking or arcing. The simple rule is that dry heat combined with airflow, as in air frying, can handle metal while electromagnetic cooking cannot.An air fryer is basically a miniature convection oven. A heating element warms the air in the chamber. A fan is used to blow hot air around the food . The speed of the air is usually between 180 and 200 degree Celsius . That moving heat sears and browns the surface of food via the Maillard reaction, the same chemical process that creates a seared steak or a golden crust on bread.A microwave oven works on a totally different principle. Rather than heating the air around food, it uses electromagnetic waves to excite water molecules within the food, generating heat from the inside.That is why microwaved leftovers tend to be soft or slightly rubbery rather than crisp – there is no dry-surface heat.This very difference is what causes metal to behave so differently in each. In an air fryer, a metal tray or foil liner just conducts and holds heat, as it does in a traditional oven. It is a passive surface. In a microwave, metal reflects electromagnetic waves rather than absorbing them. If that metal is wrinkled, jagged or too close to the cavity wall, the reflected energy can focus and arc, creating sparks that can scorch the appliance or, in rare instances, start a fire.: Foil can line the basket or wrap food directly, as long as it's weighted down by the food so it doesn't lift into the heating element and isn't covering so much surface area that it blocks airflow around the food.They’re okay, provided that they are secured by the food and don’t get caught in the fan. There are also air fryer liners, which are perforated and designed specifically for air fryers, allowing hot air to circulate around the food.: Trays, racks, and small bowls are fine for baking, roasting, or reheating, as long as they fit inside the basket without touching the heating element or blocking airflow from the fan.Oven-safe glass and ceramic dishes are fine for casseroles, small cakes, or baked dishes, as long as they're rated for high heat and sized to fit comfortably. Decorative or handmade ceramics without a heat rating are a different story. They can crack under the dry, direct heat.Food-grade silicone is good for muffins, cakes and individual portions. Small cast-iron skillets can take roasting or baking as long as both are heat-rated and don’t crowd the cooking chamber.Any item marked as microwave-safe does not necessarily mean it can be put in an air fryer, and vice versa. Both types of appliances have been tested at completely different heat levels. For instance, while a plastic container is microwaveable, it might melt under the high dry heat of an air fryer.The placement of the cookware is just as important as the cookware material itself, even if it is heat-safe.
